note: The skills catalogue. Every skill the product keeps is listed with what it is, how it is learned or shown, and what it is done with. "was" names the stored skills that became it (the first is renamed when the name is new; the rest are merged and kept as other names). "removed" lists every stored skill that is deleted, by reason. scripts/build-skills-sql.mjs turns this file into a migration that restates the whole catalogue (0033 first, 0048 after the pass that added the trades it lacked and folded brand names and course topics); a skill's group and level are in taxonomy.json, and the makes it is run on in makes.json.

skills.name: Blueprint Reading
skills.what: Reading an engineering drawing: its views, dimensions, tolerances, notes, title block and revision level. A person who has it can tell from the print exactly what part or assembly is called for and what must be checked.
skills.learned: Taught in the first term of machining, welding and drafting programs at community colleges, and in most apprenticeships. Shown by making or inspecting a part to print.

skills.name: Shop Math
skills.what: The arithmetic, fractions and decimals, unit conversion, geometry and right-angle trigonometry used at a machine or bench. A person who has it can work out a missing dimension, a bolt circle, a taper or a tolerance stack without help.
skills.learned: A first-term course in machining and tool-and-die programs; employers often test it before hiring.

skills.name: Work Instruction Reading
skills.what: Following a written work instruction, traveler or standard operating procedure step by step, including its revision, cautions and sign-offs. A person who has it builds or runs the job the same way every time and stops when the paper and the part disagree.
skills.learned: On the job in the first weeks; shown by passing an operator qualification on a station.
tools: Electronic work instructions on a station terminal

skills.name: Lot Tracking
skills.what: Keeping each lot, batch or serial number tied to its materials, process steps and results as it moves through the plant. A person who has it scans or signs every move so any part can be traced back later.
skills.learned: On the job on the plant's own system.

skills.name: Process Recipe Execution
skills.what: Selecting the qualified recipe for a lot, loading it on a process tool, starting the run and confirming it finished inside its limits. A person who has it never runs a lot on the wrong recipe and knows what to do with an aborted run.
skills.learned: On the job through tool-by-tool operator certification.

skills.name: Cleanroom Gowning
skills.what: Putting on a hood, coverall, boots, gloves and mask in the right order so skin, hair and street clothes shed nothing into a cleanroom. A person who has it can gown and de-gown without touching the outside of the garment.
skills.learned: Taught and checked on the first day in a cleanroom job; semiconductor technician programs practice it.

skills.name: Cleanroom Protocols
skills.what: Working inside a classified cleanroom without adding particles: slow movement, approved wipes, pens and paper, material wipe-down and pass-throughs. A person who has it knows the room's ISO 14644 class and what is and is not allowed in it.
skills.learned: Employer training before entry, then supervised work; covered in semiconductor and medical device technician programs.

skills.name: Aseptic Gowning Qualification
skills.what: Gowning in sterile garments for an aseptic filling area and proving it by contact plates taken from gloves and gown afterwards. A person who has it is qualified to enter the fill room and requalifies on a set schedule.
skills.learned: Site training followed by repeated qualified gownings with passing microbial results.

skills.name: ESD Control
skills.what: Handling static-sensitive parts so a discharge cannot damage them: grounding yourself and the work, and keeping parts in shielded packaging. A person who has it tests their wrist strap or footwear every shift and works only at a protected station.
skills.learned: Employer training to an ANSI/ESD S20.20 program, usually refreshed yearly; part of IPC electronics assembly courses.

skills.name: Dry Room Operations
skills.what: Working in a very low humidity room where battery electrodes and electrolyte are exposed. A person who has it keeps moisture out through airlocks, limits on people and time in the room, and watches the dew point.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: FOD Prevention
skills.what: Keeping loose hardware, tools, shavings and trash out of aircraft, engines and spacecraft. A person who has it cleans as they go, accounts for every fastener and inspects a work zone before it is closed.
skills.learned: Employer training, required before working on flight hardware and refreshed yearly.

skills.name: Tool Control
skills.what: Accounting for every tool taken to a job so none is left inside the product. A person who has it checks tools out and in, inspects a shadowed box at the start and end of a shift and reports a missing tool at once.
skills.learned: Employer training; standard practice in aircraft, engine and spacecraft work.

skills.name: Manufacturing Execution System Use
skills.what: Using a plant's MES to start and complete operations, record material and labor, and pull production data. A person who has it can find where an order stands and what happened to it at each step.
skills.learned: On the job on the plant's system.

skills.name: Overhead Crane Operation
skills.what: Running a bridge or gantry crane from a pendant or radio remote to lift, travel and set a load. A person who has it inspects the crane and hook before use, keeps the load low and under control and never lifts over people.
skills.learned: Employer training and evaluation under OSHA 1910.179; NCCCO offers an overhead crane operator certification.

skills.name: Rigging and Slinging
skills.what: Choosing and attaching slings, shackles and lifting points so a load lifts level and within rated capacity. A person who has it can estimate weight and center of gravity, read sling angle tables and inspect rigging for damage.
skills.learned: Millwright and ironworker apprenticeships; employer qualified-rigger training; NCCCO Rigger Level I and II.
tools: Wire rope, chain and synthetic slings

skills.name: Forklift Operation
skills.what: Driving a powered industrial truck to lift, carry and stack loads. A person who has it does the pre-shift check, reads the capacity plate and travels and stacks safely around people and racking.
skills.learned: Employer training and a hands-on evaluation required by OSHA 1910.178, repeated at least every three years. The employer issues the certification.

skills.name: Aerial Lift Operation
skills.what: Working from a scissor lift or boom lift. A person who has it inspects the lift before use, checks the ground and what is overhead, ties off where the lift requires it and positions the platform without striking the work.
skills.learned: Employer training and a hands-on evaluation on each type of lift, as OSHA requires; the lift makers and equipment dealers run operator courses.

skills.name: Part Marking
skills.what: Putting a permanent identity on a part: part number, serial number, lot or a data matrix code, by laser, dot peen, electrochemical etch, ink stamp or label. A person who has it marks in the place and by the method the drawing calls for and verifies that the mark reads.
skills.learned: On the job, in the first weeks at a station that marks parts.

skills.name: Shop Safety Practices
skills.what: The basic habits of working safely around machines: guards in place, eye and hearing protection, no loose clothing, clear aisles, knowing the emergency stops and reporting hazards. A person who has it can be left at a machine without being a danger to themselves or others.
skills.learned: Employer orientation and the first weeks of any trade program. An OSHA 10-hour General Industry outreach card shows the basics.

skills.name: Lockout Tagout
skills.what: Shutting equipment down and locking out every energy source, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, gravity and stored, before putting hands in it. A person who has it applies their own lock and tag, releases stored energy and tries the start before work begins.
skills.learned: Employer training as an authorized employee under OSHA 1910.147, with a yearly check of each procedure.

skills.name: Electrical Safety
skills.what: Recognizing shock and arc-flash hazards and working so neither can reach you. A person who has it reads an arc-flash label, tests for absence of voltage before touching and wears the rated protective equipment for the task.
skills.learned: Employer qualified-person training built on NFPA 70E, refreshed at least every three years.

skills.name: High Voltage Safety
skills.what: Working safely on battery packs and drive systems that stay energized and cannot simply be switched off. A person who has it uses insulated tools and gloves, respects approach limits and verifies isolation before touching a conductor.
skills.learned: Employer high-voltage qualification, usually in levels, built on NFPA 70E practice.

skills.name: Chemical Safety
skills.what: Handling acids, solvents, resins and process chemicals without exposure or a spill. A person who has it reads the label and safety data sheet first, uses the right gloves and ventilation and knows where the eyewash and shower are.
skills.learned: Employer hazard communication training under OSHA 1910.1200 before first exposure.
tools: Chemical-resistant gloves, aprons and face shields

skills.name: Safety Data Sheet Reading
skills.what: Finding what matters in a safety data sheet: hazards, required protection, first aid, storage and what the chemical must not be mixed with. A person who has it can look up any chemical on site and act on what the sheet says.
skills.learned: Part of hazard communication training under OSHA 1910.1200.

skills.name: PPE Selection
skills.what: Choosing and wearing the right protective equipment for a task, by hazard: impact, chemical splash, heat, noise, cuts. A person who has it knows the limits of each item and checks it before use.
skills.learned: Employer training tied to the hazard assessment required by OSHA 1910.132.
tools: Safety glasses, goggles and face shields

skills.name: Hazardous Materials Handling
skills.what: Receiving, storing, moving and disposing of hazardous materials and waste under the rules that apply. A person who has it segregates incompatibles, labels containers and completes the paperwork correctly.
skills.learned: Employer training; DOT hazmat employee training (49 CFR 172.704, every three years) for shipping, and OSHA HAZWOPER (1910.120) for spill response and waste sites.

skills.name: Specialty Gas Handling
skills.what: Working with toxic, corrosive, flammable and pyrophoric process gases such as silane, chlorine and arsine. A person who has it changes cylinders in a gas cabinet with the correct purge cycles and responds properly to a gas alarm.
skills.learned: Employer training at a fab or gas supplier, with supervised cylinder changes before working alone.
tools: Gas cabinets and valve manifold boxes

skills.name: Laser Safety
skills.what: Working around Class 3B and Class 4 industrial lasers without eye or skin injury. A person who has it knows the laser class and wavelength, wears matching eyewear when a beam is open and never defeats an enclosure interlock.
skills.learned: Employer training under an ANSI Z136.1 program run by the site's Laser Safety Officer.

skills.name: Radiation Safety
skills.what: Keeping radiation dose as low as reasonably achievable around X-ray tubes and gamma sources by time, distance and shielding. A person who has it wears and reads dosimetry, sets up boundaries and surveys the area before and after an exposure.
skills.learned: Radiation safety training required by the state or NRC license. Radiographers using gamma sources must hold a radiographer certification such as ASNT IRRSP or a state card.

skills.name: Robot Cell Safety
skills.what: Entering and working in a robot cell without being struck or trapped. A person who has it uses the gate interlock and their own lock, carries the teach pendant with the enabling switch and understands the cell's safeguarded space.
skills.learned: Employer training based on ANSI/RIA R15.06; robot makers include it in their operator courses.

skills.name: Hydraulic Safety
skills.what: Working on hydraulic systems without injury from stored pressure, hot oil or a pinhole leak. A person who has it bleeds accumulators and blocks loads before opening a line and never feels for a leak by hand.
skills.learned: Covered in fluid power courses and maintenance apprenticeships; reinforced by employer lockout training.

skills.name: Composite Material Safety
skills.what: Protecting skin and lungs when cutting, sanding and curing composites. A person who has it controls carbon and glass dust at the source and handles resins and hardeners, which can sensitize skin, with the right gloves.
skills.learned: Employer training; covered in composite technician programs.

skills.name: Metal Powder Handling
skills.what: Loading, sieving and recovering fine metal and polymer powders for additive manufacturing. A person who has it controls dust, grounds equipment against static and treats reactive powders such as aluminum and titanium as a fire and explosion hazard.
skills.learned: Machine maker and employer training before running a powder-bed printer.

skills.name: Ordnance Handling
skills.what: Handling, moving and installing explosive devices such as initiators, rocket motors and warheads. A person who has it follows quantity and distance limits, grounds themselves and the item and uses only approved tools.
skills.learned: Employer explosives safety certification on a defense or space program, renewed on a schedule.

skills.name: Confined Space Entry
skills.what: Entering tanks, pits, vessels and ducts that have limited access and may hold a bad atmosphere. A person who has it works to an entry permit, tests the air first, keeps an attendant outside and knows the rescue plan.
skills.learned: Employer training as entrant, attendant or supervisor under OSHA 1910.146.

skills.name: Fall Protection
skills.what: Working at height tied off so a fall is stopped before injury. A person who has it inspects a harness and lanyard, picks a rated anchor and knows the clearance a fall needs.
skills.learned: Employer training; required by OSHA whenever fall protection is used.

skills.name: Respiratory Protection
skills.what: Using a respirator correctly where paint, solvent, dust or fume cannot be controlled at the source. A person who has it picks the right cartridge, does a seal check each time and keeps the mask clean and stored.
skills.learned: Medical clearance, training and a yearly fit test under OSHA 1910.134.

skills.name: CNC Control Operation
skills.what: Working a CNC machine's control: loading and proving out a program, jogging, setting modes and overrides, reading alarms and restarting safely mid-program. A person who has it can run a job on the control without a setup person standing by.
skills.learned: Machining programs at community colleges and on the job; NIMS CNC Milling and CNC Turning Operations credentials cover it.
tools: Program transfer by network, USB or DNC

skills.name: Tool and Work Offsets
skills.what: Telling the machine where the part and each tool are: touching off tools, setting work coordinates such as G54 and adjusting wear offsets to hold size. A person who has it can bring a part back into tolerance from a measurement without editing the program.
skills.learned: Machining programs and on the job; part of NIMS CNC setup credentials.

skills.name: Workholding and Fixturing
skills.what: Holding a part so it cannot move and is not distorted while it is cut. A person who has it chooses and sets up vises, chucks, soft jaws, collets, clamps and fixtures, and indicates the part true before cutting.
skills.learned: Machining programs and apprenticeships; on the job.

skills.name: Speeds and Feeds Calculation
skills.what: Working out spindle speed, feed rate and depth of cut from the material, the cutter and the machine. A person who has it can set starting values from surface speed and chip load, then adjust them by the sound, chips and finish.
skills.learned: A core topic in machining programs; tested in NIMS machining credentials.

skills.name: G-Code Programming
skills.what: Writing and editing CNC programs by hand in G and M code: moves, canned cycles, cutter compensation and subprograms. A person who has it can read any program at the control and fix or shorten it.
skills.learned: Machining programs at community colleges; NIMS CNC Milling and Turning Programming, Setup and Operations credentials.

skills.name: CAM Programming
skills.what: Building CNC toolpaths from a 3D model in CAM software, choosing tools and strategies, simulating the cut and posting code for a specific machine. A person who has it can take a part from model to proven program.
skills.learned: Community-college CNC programming courses; the CAM software makers certify users; on the job.

skills.name: CNC Milling
skills.what: Setting up and running vertical and horizontal machining centers: loading tools, setting offsets, running first parts and holding dimensions through a lot. A person who has it works from a setup sheet and corrects for tool wear.
skills.learned: Machining programs and on the job; NIMS CNC Milling credentials.
tools: End mills, drills and face mills

skills.name: Multi-Axis Turning
skills.what: Running CNC lathes with live tooling, a Y axis and sub-spindles, so a part is turned, milled and drilled complete in one machine. A person who has it can set up both spindles and time the handoff between them.
skills.learned: On the job after basic CNC turning; machine makers' courses. NIMS CNC Turning credentials cover the basics.

skills.name: Swiss-Type Machining
skills.what: Running a sliding-headstock lathe, where bar stock feeds through a guide bushing past the tools, to make long, small, precise parts. A person who has it sets guide bushing tension, bar feeder and gang tools and holds tenths over a long run.
skills.learned: On the job in a screw-machine shop; machine makers' training.

skills.name: 5-Axis Machining
skills.what: Setting up and running machines that tilt and rotate the part or spindle so complex surfaces are cut in one clamping. A person who has it sets the rotary center, uses tool center point control and checks for collisions before cutting.
skills.learned: On the job after three-axis experience; advanced CNC courses and machine makers' training.

skills.name: Manual Lathe Operation
skills.what: Turning, facing, boring, grooving and single-point threading on an engine lathe by hand. A person who has it can make a round part to a thousandth from a drawing.
skills.learned: The first machine taught in machining programs and apprenticeships; NIMS Turning credentials.

skills.name: Manual Mill Operation
skills.what: Squaring stock, milling steps and pockets, drilling and boring holes to position on a knee mill. A person who has it trams the head, indicates a vise and works to a thousandth with the dials or readout.
skills.learned: Machining programs and apprenticeships; NIMS Milling credential.

skills.name: Precision Grinding
skills.what: Finishing hardened parts to tenths of a thousandth and a fine surface on surface, cylindrical and centerless grinders. A person who has it picks the wheel, controls heat and checks size and finish as they go.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die and machining apprenticeships; NIMS Grinding credential.

skills.name: Grinding Wheel Dressing
skills.what: Truing a grinding wheel so it runs round and dressing it so it cuts freely, including forming a radius or profile on the wheel. A person who has it also ring-tests and mounts wheels safely.
skills.learned: Learned with precision grinding, in apprenticeships and on the job.

skills.name: Jig Grinding
skills.what: Grinding holes and contours to very exact size and position in hardened tooling. A person who has it locates features within tenths and finishes die and gauge details that other machines cannot.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die apprenticeship, late in training; on the job.

skills.name: Honing and Lapping
skills.what: Bringing bores and flat faces to final size, geometry and finish with abrasive stones or loose abrasive on a lap. A person who has it can hold a bore straight and round within tenths and lap a face flat to light bands.
skills.learned: On the job in gauge, hydraulic and toolroom work.

skills.name: Wire EDM
skills.what: Cutting hardened metal with an electrically charged wire to make punches, dies and fine profiles. A person who has it threads and aligns the wire, sets power and flushing and plans skim cuts for size and finish.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die apprenticeships and on the job; machine makers' training. NIMS offers EDM credentials.

skills.name: Sinker EDM
skills.what: Burning a cavity into hardened metal with a shaped electrode. A person who has it makes and mounts electrodes, sets overburn, flushing and power, and orbits to final size and finish.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die and moldmaking apprenticeships; NIMS offers EDM credentials.

skills.name: Isogrid Machining
skills.what: Milling triangular or square pocket patterns into thick plate to leave thin skins and stiffening ribs for tanks and fuselage panels. A person who has it controls rib and skin thickness on a large, flexible part that moves as it is cut.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerospace structures plant.

skills.name: Structural Casting Machining
skills.what: Machining mounting faces, holes and datums on large aluminum die castings such as vehicle underbodies. A person who has it fixtures a thin, slightly warped casting without distorting it and holds positions across its length.
skills.learned: On the job at a casting plant, after general CNC experience.
tools: Large horizontal and gantry machining centers

skills.name: Deburring and Hand Finishing
skills.what: Removing burrs and sharp edges and blending tool marks by hand after machining. A person who has it breaks every edge to the drawing's note without changing a dimension, rounding a sealing surface or scratching a finished face.
skills.learned: On the job in the first weeks in a machine shop; machining programs teach benchwork in the first term.

skills.name: Drilling and Tapping
skills.what: Making and threading holes on a drill press or by hand: center, drill, ream, countersink, tap and chase. A person who has it picks the tap drill from a chart, keeps a tap square, clears chips and does not break a tap in the part.
skills.learned: Taught with the first machines in machining programs and apprenticeships; on the job.
tools: Taps, tap wrenches and tapping heads

skills.name: CNC Turning
skills.what: Setting up and running CNC lathes and turning centers: chuck jaws or collets, turret tools, offsets, first part and dimensions held through a lot. A person who has it bores soft jaws, sets tools on center and corrects diameters for tool wear and taper.
skills.learned: Machining programs and on the job; NIMS CNC Turning credentials.
tools: Turning, boring, grooving and threading tools

skills.name: Cutting Tool Presetting
skills.what: Assembling cutting tools in their holders and measuring them off the machine, so a job starts with known lengths and diameters. A person who has it builds a tool to the tool list, measures it on a presetter, sends the offsets to the control and tracks tool life.
skills.learned: On the job in a tool crib or as a setup machinist; presetter makers' courses.
tools: Shrink-fit and hydraulic holders, collet chucks
Tool assembly fixtures and torque wrenches

skills.name: On-Machine Probing
skills.what: Using the spindle probe and tool setter of a CNC machine to find the part, set work offsets, measure features between cuts and check for broken tools. A person who has it calibrates the probe, runs the probing cycles and knows when a probed number can be trusted.
skills.learned: On the job as a setup machinist; probe makers' courses.
tools: Tool setters and laser tool setters

skills.name: MIG Welding
skills.what: Gas metal arc welding: a wire fed through a gun under shielding gas. A person who has it sets voltage, wire speed and gas for the joint and lays sound fillet and groove welds in flat, horizontal, vertical and overhead positions.
skills.learned: Community-college welding programs and apprenticeships. Shown by a welder qualification test, most often to AWS D1.1 for structural steel.
tools: GMAW power sources and wire feeders

skills.name: TIG Welding
skills.what: Gas tungsten arc welding: an arc from a tungsten electrode with filler added by hand. A person who has it controls heat with a foot pedal or torch control and makes clean, precise welds on thin and critical parts.
skills.learned: Welding programs, usually after MIG and stick. Shown by a qualification test to the code the work falls under, such as AWS D17.1 for aerospace or ASME Section IX for pressure work.

skills.name: Stick Welding
skills.what: Shielded metal arc welding with flux-coated electrodes. A person who has it strikes and holds an arc, runs E6010 and E7018 rod in all positions and welds outdoors and on dirty or heavy steel.
skills.learned: Welding programs and apprenticeships. Shown by a plate or pipe qualification test, commonly to AWS D1.1.

skills.name: Flux-Cored Welding
skills.what: Wire welding with a flux-filled wire, with or without shielding gas, for high deposition on thicker steel. A person who has it sets the machine for the wire, controls slag and runs out-of-position welds.
skills.learned: Welding programs and structural shops. Shown by an AWS D1.1 qualification test.

skills.name: Aluminum Welding
skills.what: Welding aluminum alloys by TIG or MIG. A person who has it cleans oxide before welding, manages the metal's fast heat flow, picks 4043 or 5356 filler and avoids porosity and crater cracks.
skills.learned: Welding programs after steel; on the job. Qualification tests are to AWS D1.2 for structures or AWS D17.1 for aerospace.

skills.name: Stainless Steel Welding
skills.what: Welding stainless steels so the joint keeps its strength and corrosion resistance. A person who has it limits heat input, back-purges the root and picks filler to match the grade.
skills.learned: Welding programs and on the job. Qualification tests are to AWS D1.6, AWS D17.1 or ASME Section IX depending on the work.

skills.name: Titanium Welding
skills.what: TIG welding titanium, which is ruined by air while hot. A person who has it shields the weld and the cooling metal with argon and judges the result by weld color.
skills.learned: On the job in aerospace and medical work after TIG experience; qualification to AWS D17.1.

skills.name: Aluminum-Lithium Welding
skills.what: Joining aluminum-lithium and 2219 alloys used for launch vehicle tanks, by fusion or friction stir welding. A person who has it prepares the joint to remove the oxide layer and controls the porosity and cracking these alloys are prone to.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch vehicle plant; qualification to AWS D17.1 or the builder's own specification.
tools: Variable polarity TIG and plasma equipment

skills.name: Pipe Welding
skills.what: Welding pipe joints that cannot be turned, in fixed positions up to 6G. A person who has it puts in an open root and fills and caps it to pass X-ray or a bend test.
skills.learned: Welding programs and pipefitter apprenticeships. Shown by a pipe qualification test to ASME Section IX or API 1104.

skills.name: Orbital Welding
skills.what: Automatic TIG welding of tube and pipe with a head that travels around the joint. A person who has it prepares square tube ends, programs the weld schedule and judges the finished bead inside and out.
skills.learned: Equipment makers' courses and on the job in semiconductor, pharmaceutical and aerospace tubing work, which follow ASME BPE or the customer's specification.
tools: Orbital weld heads and power supplies

skills.name: Cryogenic Tank Welding
skills.what: Welding propellant and cryogenic tanks that must stay leak-tight and tough at very low temperature. A person who has it holds fit-up and heat input on long seams and welds to X-ray quality.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch vehicle or pressure vessel plant after proven TIG or automatic welding experience.

skills.name: Pressure Vessel Fabrication
skills.what: Forming, fitting and welding the shells, domes and fittings of a pressure vessel and preparing it for proof test. A person who has it works to the code or specification the vessel is built under and keeps the weld and material records it requires.
skills.learned: On the job at a code shop or spacecraft plant; welders qualify to ASME Section IX or AWS D17.1.
tools: Proof test and leak test equipment

skills.name: Electron Beam Welding
skills.what: Welding in a vacuum chamber with a focused beam of electrons, for deep, narrow welds in reactive and thick metals. A person who has it fixtures the part, aligns the beam to the joint and sets beam current, focus and travel speed.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerospace or engine plant; operators qualify to AWS D17.1.

skills.name: Laser Welding
skills.what: Joining metal with a focused laser, by hand-fed optics or more often a robot. A person who has it sets power, focus position, speed and shielding gas, keeps optics clean and reads a weld for undercut, porosity and lack of fusion.
skills.learned: On the job and through laser makers' courses, after laser safety training.

skills.name: Laser Brazing
skills.what: Joining sheet with a laser-melted filler wire that flows into the seam without melting the panels, as on a car roof joint. A person who has it sets wire feed, laser power and tracking so the seam is smooth enough to paint.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive body shop.
tools: Laser brazing heads with tactile seam tracking

skills.name: Friction Stir Welding
skills.what: Joining aluminum without melting it, by a rotating pin that stirs the two edges together. A person who has it sets tool speed, travel and force, clamps the joint rigidly and inspects for voids and lack of penetration.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerospace, rail or battery enclosure plant; AWS D17.3 covers aerospace aluminum work.

skills.name: Resistance Spot Welding
skills.what: Joining overlapped sheet by squeezing it between copper electrodes and passing current. A person who has it sets current, time and force for the stack-up and checks nugget size.
skills.learned: On the job in automotive and sheet metal plants; AWS D8.1M covers automotive weld quality and AWS D17.2 aerospace work.

skills.name: Robotic Spot Welding
skills.what: Running a robot spot welding cell: weld schedules, gun and tip condition, and the position of every weld on the part. A person who has it recovers from faults, touches up weld points and keeps weld quality between tip changes.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive body shop, with robot maker training.

skills.name: Spot Weld Tip Dressing
skills.what: Restoring the face of spot weld electrodes as they mushroom and pick up coating, and changing them when worn. A person who has it sets dress frequency and checks the dressed tip so welds stay full size.
skills.learned: On the job in a body shop.

skills.name: Weld Joint Fit-Up
skills.what: Preparing and assembling parts for welding: bevel, root opening, alignment and tacks. A person who has it sets a joint to the welding procedure and allows for the distortion the weld will cause.
skills.learned: Welding and fabrication programs; on the job.

skills.name: Weld Symbol Interpretation
skills.what: Reading the welding symbols on a drawing: weld type, size, length, side, contour and any testing called for. A person who has it knows what weld goes where without asking.
skills.learned: Taught with blueprint reading in welding programs. The symbols are defined in AWS A2.4.

skills.name: Visual Weld Inspection
skills.what: Examining a finished weld by eye and gauge for size, profile, undercut, porosity, cracks and overlap against the acceptance criteria of the code. A person who has it can accept or reject a weld and say why.
skills.learned: Welding programs and on the job. The AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) is the recognized credential for inspectors.

skills.name: Destructive Weld Testing
skills.what: Proving a weld by breaking it: bend tests, peel and chisel tests on spot welds, pull tests and cut-and-etch sections. A person who has it prepares the sample, runs the test and reads the result against the standard.
skills.learned: On the job in a weld lab or body shop; welding programs teach the guided bend test.

skills.name: Weld Procedure Qualification
skills.what: Writing a welding procedure specification and proving it with a test weld recorded on a procedure qualification record. A person who has it knows the essential variables of the code and what change requires requalifying.
skills.learned: On the job as a welding engineer or lead; AWS CWI training covers the code rules. AWS D1.1, AWS D17.1 and ASME Section IX each set their own requirements.

skills.name: Welder Performance Qualification
skills.what: Passing a welding test to a code: welding a coupon in a set position, process and thickness that then passes visual and bend or X-ray examination. A person who has it is qualified for that range of work and keeps the qualification current by welding with the process.
skills.learned: Tested by an employer or an AWS Accredited Test Facility, which can issue AWS Certified Welder cards. Tests are commonly to AWS D1.1 or ASME Section IX.

skills.name: Oxy-Fuel Cutting
skills.what: Cutting steel with an oxygen and fuel gas torch. A person who has it sets up and leak-checks regulators and hoses, lights and adjusts the flame and makes a clean, square cut by hand or on a track.
skills.learned: Taught at the start of welding programs.

skills.name: Plasma Cutting
skills.what: Cutting steel, stainless and aluminum with a plasma arc, by hand or on a CNC table. A person who has it sets amperage, gas and cut height for the material and replaces consumables before cut quality drops.
skills.learned: Welding and fabrication programs; on the job.

skills.name: Laser Cutting
skills.what: Cutting sheet and plate on a CNC laser. A person who has it loads nests, sets focus, assist gas and power for the material and thickness, and keeps nozzle and lens in condition for a clean edge.
skills.learned: On the job; machine makers' courses.

skills.name: Abrasive Waterjet Cutting
skills.what: Cutting metal, composite and stone with a high-pressure water stream carrying garnet abrasive, with no heat-affected edge. A person who has it sets pressure, abrasive flow and speed for edge quality and maintains the pump, orifice and mixing tube.
skills.learned: On the job; machine makers' courses.

skills.name: Press Brake Operation
skills.what: Bending sheet metal to angle and dimension on a press brake. A person who has it picks punch and die, sets the back gauge, works out bend order and allowance and checks the first part.
skills.learned: On the job and in fabrication programs; the Fabricators & Manufacturers Association offers a Precision Sheet Metal Operator certification.

skills.name: Sheet Metal Forming
skills.what: Shaping sheet and plate by shearing, bending, rolling and hand forming. A person who has it can turn a flat blank into a finished shape without cracking or marking it.
skills.learned: Sheet metal apprenticeships and fabrication programs.

skills.name: Sheet Metal Layout
skills.what: Developing a flat pattern from a drawing, with bend allowances, and marking it on the sheet. A person who has it lays out cones, transitions and boxes that fold to size.
skills.learned: Sheet metal apprenticeships and fabrication programs; CAD unfolding is learned on the job.

skills.name: Structural Steel Fabrication
skills.what: Cutting, drilling, fitting and welding beams, columns and plate into structural members to shop drawings. A person who has it lays out from the drawing, holds length and squareness and prepares joints for field assembly.
skills.learned: Ironworker and fitter apprenticeships; on the job in a structural shop working to AWS D1.1.

skills.name: Tube Bending and Flaring
skills.what: Cutting, bending and finishing rigid tube for fluid lines: bends without wrinkles or flattening, and flared, beaded or swaged ends that seal. A person who has it can make a line that fits from a drawing or a sample.
skills.learned: On the job in aerospace and hydraulic work; aviation maintenance schools teach it.

skills.name: Robotic Arc Welding
skills.what: Running a robot arc welding cell: loading parts in the fixture, touching up weld points, adjusting wire feed, voltage and travel speed, and keeping torch, tip and liner in condition. A person who has it reads the welds coming off the cell and corrects the program or the fit-up before bad parts stack up.
skills.learned: On the job after manual MIG welding; robot and welding equipment makers' operator courses. AWS certifies robotic arc welding operators and technicians (CRAW).
tools: Welding power sources and wire feeders

skills.name: Torch Brazing
skills.what: Joining metal with a filler that melts below the base metal, heated by a torch or an induction coil. A person who has it cleans and fits the joint to the right gap, fluxes it, heats evenly so the filler is drawn through by capillary action and cleans off the residue.
skills.learned: HVAC, plumbing and welding programs; on the job. Brazers are qualified to ASME Section IX or AWS B2.2.

skills.name: Furnace Brazing
skills.what: Brazing whole assemblies in a vacuum or controlled-atmosphere furnace, where every joint flows at once. A person who has it applies filler and stop-off, fixtures the assembly so gaps hold at temperature, runs the cycle and inspects the joints for flow and voids.
skills.learned: On the job in a brazing shop, usually after torch brazing or heat treat work. Aerospace work is done to AWS C3.6 and audited under Nadcap.
tools: Nickel, gold and copper braze alloys as paste, foil and wire

skills.name: Die Setting
skills.what: Installing a stamping die in a press: moving it in, locating and clamping it, setting shut height, feed and sensors, and running first hits. A person who has it changes a press over safely and hands it to production making good parts.
skills.learned: On the job in a stamping plant, moving up from press operator; the Precision Metalforming Association offers die-setter training.

skills.name: Progressive Die Operation
skills.what: Running a press where coil stock steps through a series of stations in one die. A person who has it threads the strip, sets feed length and pilot release and watches for misfeeds, slug pulls and burrs.
skills.learned: On the job in a stamping plant.
tools: Coil reels, straighteners and servo feeds

skills.name: Transfer Die Operation
skills.what: Running a press line where fingers or robots carry each blank from die to die for drawing, trimming, flanging and piercing. A person who has it sets transfer timing and grippers and clears a mis-hit without damaging the dies.
skills.learned: On the job in a stamping plant.

skills.name: Draw Die Operation
skills.what: Forming a deep shape from a flat blank in a draw die. A person who has it adjusts binder pressure, lubrication and blank position to stop splits and wrinkles.
skills.learned: On the job in a stamping plant, usually after experience as a press operator.

skills.name: Die Tryout
skills.what: Proving a new or repaired die in a press until it makes parts to print. A person who has it reads splits, wrinkles, springback and burrs on a panel and decides what to change in the die.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die apprenticeship followed by years on the tryout floor.

skills.name: Die Spotting
skills.what: Fitting the mating faces of a die so they bear evenly, by closing them with marking compound and grinding the high spots. A person who has it brings a die to full contact without losing the form.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die apprenticeship; on the job in a die shop.

skills.name: Die Component Fitting
skills.what: Fitting and timing the working parts of a die: punches, buttons, pilots, strippers, cams and springs. A person who has it sets clearances and replaces worn details so the die cuts cleanly.
skills.learned: Tool-and-die apprenticeship; on the job in die maintenance.

skills.name: Stamped Panel Inspection
skills.what: Checking a stamped panel for splits, wrinkles, thinning, burrs and surface lows and highs. A person who has it stones a panel to show surface defects and checks it on a fixture against trim and hole positions.
skills.learned: On the job in a stamping plant.

skills.name: Hemming
skills.what: Folding the edge of an outer panel over an inner panel to make doors, hoods and decklids. A person who has it sets pre-hem and final hem by die or roller so the edge is tight and the surface shows no marks.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive body shop.

skills.name: Metal Spin Forming
skills.what: Shaping a round blank over a rotating mandrel into a dome, cone or cylinder. A person who has it works the metal in passes without thinning or wrinkling it and anneals when it hardens.
skills.learned: On the job in a spinning shop or tank plant.

skills.name: Die Casting Machine Operation
skills.what: Running a high-pressure die casting cell through its cycle: ladle, shot, cooling, extraction, spray. A person who has it watches shot curves and die temperatures and sorts castings for cold shuts, flash and porosity.
skills.learned: On the job; the North American Die Casting Association offers operator courses.

skills.name: Die Casting Shot Control
skills.what: Setting how molten metal is pushed into the die: slow shot, fast shot, changeover point and intensification pressure. A person who has it reads the shot trace and adjusts it to cut porosity and misruns.
skills.learned: On the job, moving up from machine operator; North American Die Casting Association courses.

skills.name: Vacuum Die Casting
skills.what: Die casting with the air pulled from the cavity before the shot so structural castings come out with little trapped gas. A person who has it keeps vacuum channels, valves and seals working and reads the vacuum level each cycle.
skills.learned: On the job at a structural casting plant.
tools: Vacuum units, chill vents and valves

skills.name: Die Lubricant Spray Setup
skills.what: Setting where, how long and how much release agent is sprayed on a casting die each cycle. A person who has it balances die temperature and release so castings neither solder to the die nor carry gas from excess spray.
skills.learned: On the job in a die casting plant.

skills.name: Die Casting Die Setup and Maintenance
skills.what: Installing a casting die, connecting its cooling, vacuum and hydraulic lines, and keeping it running. A person who has it changes inserts and ejector pins, cleans vents and polishes out soldering.
skills.learned: On the job, often after a tool-and-die or maintenance background.

skills.name: Casting Trimming
skills.what: Removing gates, runners, overflows and flash from a casting in a trim press or by saw and robot. A person who has it sets the trim die and checks that nothing is left on, or cut into, the part.
skills.learned: On the job in a casting plant.

skills.name: Aluminum Melt Preparation
skills.what: Melting and holding casting alloy at the right chemistry, temperature and cleanliness. A person who has it charges the furnace, degasses and fluxes the melt and takes samples for chemistry and density.
skills.learned: On the job in a foundry or die casting plant.

skills.name: Metal 3D Printing
skills.what: Building metal parts layer by layer, most often by laser powder bed fusion. A person who has it sets up the build plate and recoater, loads powder, starts and monitors the build and removes it safely.
skills.learned: Machine makers' training and on the job; some community colleges teach additive manufacturing. SME offers additive manufacturing certifications.

skills.name: Polymer 3D Printing
skills.what: Printing plastic parts by filament extrusion, resin curing or powder sintering. A person who has it picks the process and material, orients the part, tunes settings and clears supports.
skills.learned: Community-college and maker programs; on the job. SME offers additive manufacturing certifications.

skills.name: Additive Build Preparation
skills.what: Preparing a 3D printing job: repairing the model, orienting and nesting parts, adding supports and slicing. A person who has it lays out a build that prints first time and is easy to remove.
skills.learned: On the job; software makers' training.

skills.name: Additive Part Post-Processing
skills.what: Finishing printed parts: depowdering, stress relief, cutting from the build plate, removing supports and finishing surfaces. A person who has it brings a raw build to a part that meets drawing.
skills.learned: On the job in an additive shop.

skills.name: Design for Additive Manufacturing
skills.what: Designing parts to be printed: self-supporting angles, wall thickness, internal channels, lattice and build orientation. A person who has it can redesign a machined or cast part to print reliably and use less material.
skills.learned: Engineering courses and on the job; SME and ASTM offer additive manufacturing training.
tools: CAD with lattice and topology tools

skills.name: Hot Isostatic Pressing
skills.what: Closing internal porosity in castings and printed parts with high temperature and gas pressure in a pressure vessel. A person who has it loads parts, runs the specified cycle and reviews the temperature and pressure record.
skills.learned: On the job at a HIP supplier or a plant with its own unit.

skills.name: Injection Molding Machine Operation
skills.what: Running an injection molding press through production: keeping material fed and dried, checking parts for short shots, flash, sink and splay, trimming gates and packing. A person who has it knows the press's normal cycle and stops it when the parts or the sound change.
skills.learned: On the job at a molding plant; community-college plastics programs where there are any.

skills.name: Injection Mold Setup
skills.what: Changing a mold in an injection press: hanging and clamping the mold, connecting water, hydraulics and ejection, purging the barrel and bringing the process up from the setup sheet. A person who has it protects the mold on first close and has good parts running without scrapping a shift.
skills.learned: On the job, moving up from operator; mold setter and setup technician courses from plastics training providers.

skills.name: Injection Molding Process Development
skills.what: Establishing and troubleshooting a molding process from the plastic's point of view: fill, pack and hold separated, with a viscosity curve, gate-seal study and cavity balance behind the settings. A person who has it finds the cause of a defect in the data and widens the process window instead of chasing settings.
skills.learned: Scientific molding courses, such as RJG's Master Molder and Paulson's, after years as a setter or process technician.
tools: Cavity pressure sensors and process monitors

skills.name: Plastic Extrusion
skills.what: Running an extrusion line that makes profile, tube, sheet or film: feeding and drying resin, setting barrel and die temperatures, screw speed and puller speed, and holding dimensions as the line runs. A person who has it strings up the line at start and brings wall thickness in without stopping.
skills.learned: On the job at an extrusion plant.

skills.name: Blow Molding
skills.what: Making bottles and hollow parts by inflating hot plastic in a mold, from an extruded parison or a reheated preform. A person who has it sets heating, stretch and blow pressures, checks wall distribution and top load and clears a jam safely.
skills.learned: On the job at a container or beverage plant; machine makers' operator courses.
tools: Extrusion and reheat stretch blow molders

skills.name: Sand Casting
skills.what: Making castings in sand molds: preparing sand, ramming or machine-molding around a pattern, setting cores, closing the mold, pouring and shaking out. A person who has it reads a mold for a good pour and knows what a misrun, a scab and a shifted core look like.
skills.learned: On the job in a foundry; molder and coremaker apprenticeships. The American Foundry Society runs courses.
tools: Green sand and no-bake molding lines

skills.name: Investment Casting
skills.what: Making precise castings by the lost-wax process: injecting wax patterns, assembling them on a tree, building the ceramic shell dip by dip, dewaxing, firing, pouring and knocking out. A person who has it controls slurry and drying between coats and handles a shell without cracking it.
skills.learned: On the job in an investment foundry. The Investment Casting Institute runs process courses.
tools: Slurry tanks and sand rainfall or fluidized beds

skills.name: Assembly Hand Tool Use
skills.what: Using the hand and power tools of an assembly station correctly: drivers, wrenches, ratchets, pliers, crimpers and pneumatic and DC electric tools. A person who has it picks the right tool and bit, does not damage the fastener or the part and looks after the tools.
skills.learned: On the job in the first weeks; shown by passing a station qualification.

skills.name: Torque Wrench Use
skills.what: Tightening fasteners to a specified torque and sequence. A person who has it reads the value and pattern from the instruction, sets and uses click, dial and electronic wrenches correctly, checks the calibration date and marks each fastener done.
skills.learned: On the job; aviation maintenance and assembly programs teach it early.
tools: Click, beam, dial and electronic torque wrenches

skills.name: Assembly Visual Inspection
skills.what: Checking your own or another's assembly by eye against the instruction: right parts, right orientation, nothing missing, damaged or loose. A person who has it catches a defect at the station instead of passing it on.
skills.learned: On the job; workmanship standards are taught for each product.

skills.name: Assembly Rework and Repair
skills.what: Taking an assembly apart to correct a defect and rebuilding it to the same standard without causing new damage. A person who has it follows the approved rework method and records what was done.
skills.learned: On the job, after proving the original build skills; electronics rework is taught in IPC-7711/7721 courses.

skills.name: Bearing Installation
skills.what: Removing and fitting rolling bearings without damaging them. A person who has it presses on the correct ring, heats or cools parts for an interference fit, sets clearance or preload and keeps everything clean.
skills.learned: Maintenance and millwright apprenticeships; on the job in assembly.

skills.name: Press and Shrink Fitting
skills.what: Joining parts with an interference fit, by force or by heating one part and chilling the other. A person who has it checks sizes first, aligns the parts and watches the press force for a fit that is too loose or too tight.
skills.learned: On the job in powertrain, motor and aerospace assembly.
tools: Servo and hydraulic presses with force monitoring

skills.name: Dynamic Balancing
skills.what: Measuring the imbalance of a rotating part and correcting it by adding or removing weight. A person who has it mounts the rotor, reads amount and angle in one or two planes and brings it within the balance grade.
skills.learned: On the job; balancing machine makers' training.
tools: Drills and mills for material removal

skills.name: Structural Adhesive Application
skills.what: Applying structural adhesive that carries load in a vehicle body, battery pack or assembly. A person who has it checks surface condition, bead size and position and open time, and knows how the joint is cured.
skills.learned: On the job; adhesive suppliers train operators and technicians.
tools: One- and two-part epoxies and urethanes

skills.name: SPR and Flow-Drill Screw Joining
skills.what: Joining aluminum and mixed-metal sheet without welding, by self-piercing rivets, flow-drill screws or clinching. A person who has it sets the tool for the stack-up and checks head height and joint cross-sections.
skills.learned: On the job in an aluminum body shop; equipment makers' training.

skills.name: Body-in-White Framing
skills.what: Bringing the underbody, body sides and roof together in a framing station and locking the geometry with the first welds. A person who has it keeps locators, clamps and gates in condition so every body comes out on dimension.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive body shop.

skills.name: Panel Gap and Flush Fitting
skills.what: Hanging and adjusting doors, hoods, lids and fenders so gaps are even and surfaces sit flush. A person who has it measures, shims and adjusts hinges and strikers to the build specification.
skills.learned: On the job in body and final assembly.

skills.name: Powertrain Marriage
skills.what: Raising the drive unit, battery or engine and subframe into the body and fastening them at the marriage station. A person who has it aligns the carriers, runs the fasteners in sequence and confirms every joint is recorded.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.
tools: Lift carriers and automated guided vehicles

skills.name: Cockpit Module Installation
skills.what: Loading a built-up instrument panel into the vehicle, locating and fastening it and connecting its harnesses and ducts. A person who has it uses the assist arm without marking trim and confirms every connector is seated.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Seat Installation
skills.what: Loading seats into the vehicle, fastening them to torque and connecting airbag, heater and sensor plugs. A person who has it treats seat fasteners as safety-critical and confirms each one is recorded.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Vehicle HVAC Module Installation
skills.what: Installing a vehicle's heating and cooling module, lines and ducts and connecting them without leaks. A person who has it seats line fittings and seals correctly and keeps the system clean and capped until charge.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle assembly.

skills.name: Glass Bonding
skills.what: Bonding windshields and fixed glass to the body with urethane. A person who has it primes glass and flange, lays a continuous bead of the right shape and sets the glass to gap and height.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle assembly.

skills.name: Vehicle Fluid Fill
skills.what: Filling a new vehicle's brake, coolant, refrigerant and washer systems by evacuating each circuit, leak-checking it and filling to quantity. A person who has it connects the adapters, reads a failed vacuum decay and reworks the leak.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Vehicle Harness Routing
skills.what: Laying a wiring harness into a vehicle body along its path, clipping it and seating every connector. A person who has it keeps the harness away from edges and moving parts and confirms each connector locks.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle assembly.

skills.name: Wheel Alignment
skills.what: Setting toe, camber and caster on a new vehicle at the alignment station and centering the steering wheel. A person who has it reads the machine, makes the adjustments and torques the locking fasteners.
skills.learned: On the job at the end of a vehicle assembly line.

skills.name: Solid Rivet Installation
skills.what: Driving solid rivets in aircraft structure with a rivet gun and bucking bar or a squeezer. A person who has it picks rivet length, sets air pressure, forms a shop head to size and removes a bad rivet without enlarging the hole.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and aerospace manufacturing programs; on the job with a training panel test.

skills.name: Blind Rivet Installation
skills.what: Installing blind rivets and blind bolts where the back of the joint cannot be reached. A person who has it selects grip length from the stack-up, pulls the fastener and checks stem break and collar position.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and on the job.

skills.name: Hi-Lok Fastener Installation
skills.what: Installing threaded pin-and-collar fasteners in aircraft structure. A person who has it checks hole size and grip, seats the pin, runs the collar until its wrenching element shears off and verifies pin protrusion.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerostructures plant after basic drilling and riveting; employers test on a sample panel.

skills.name: Lockbolt Installation
skills.what: Installing lockbolts, where a collar is swaged onto a grooved pin by a pulling tool. A person who has it selects grip, checks collar swage with a gauge and removes a bad one without damaging structure.
skills.learned: On the job; aviation maintenance schools.
tools: Pneumatic-hydraulic pulling tools and nose assemblies

skills.name: Nutplate Installation
skills.what: Fitting riveted or bonded anchor nuts so a screw can be installed where the back is closed off. A person who has it drills the rivet pattern with a drill jig, countersinks and rivets the nutplate without distorting it.
skills.learned: On the job; aviation maintenance schools.

skills.name: Threaded Insert Installation
skills.what: Installing wire-coil and key-locking thread inserts to give strong threads in soft metal or to repair damaged ones. A person who has it drills and taps to the insert's size, sets it to depth and breaks off the tang or drives the keys.
skills.learned: On the job in machining, assembly and repair.

skills.name: Fastener Hole Drilling and Reaming
skills.what: Drilling, reaming and deburring fastener holes in aircraft structure to size, position and squareness. A person who has it steps a hole up to final size, uses drill guides and checks it with a hole gauge.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and aerospace assembly programs; on the job.

skills.name: Countersinking
skills.what: Cutting a countersink so a flush fastener sits level with the skin. A person who has it sets a stop-controlled cutter to depth on scrap first and checks flushness on the part.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and on the job.

skills.name: Cold Expansion of Fastener Holes
skills.what: Pulling an oversize mandrel through a hole to leave compressive stress around it, so the structure resists fatigue cracks. A person who has it checks starting hole size, pulls the mandrel and sleeve, reams to final size and verifies expansion.
skills.learned: On the job, with tooling supplier training.

skills.name: Aerospace Fastener Identification
skills.what: Recognizing aircraft fasteners by part number, head marking, material and finish, and choosing the right diameter and grip length. A person who has it never substitutes a fastener and can read AN, MS and NAS callouts.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools; on the job.

skills.name: Shimming
skills.what: Measuring the gap between mating structure and filling it so fasteners do not pull parts out of shape. A person who has it picks solid, laminated or liquid shim by gap size and the limits in the specification.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerostructures plant.

skills.name: Aerospace Sealant Application
skills.what: Mixing and applying two-part sealants to aircraft joints and fasteners: faying surface, fillet, brush coat and wet installation. A person who has it cleans the surface, works within the application life and leaves a bead with no voids.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerostructures plant; employers certify sealers.

skills.name: Safety Wire Installation
skills.what: Securing bolts, plugs and connectors with twisted wire so they cannot loosen. A person who has it routes the wire to pull in the tightening direction, twists it evenly and leaves a neat pigtail.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and on the job; NASM33540 sets the practice.

skills.name: Major Structural Join
skills.what: Joining large aircraft sections, fuselage barrels or wing to body: aligning them, drilling the join and installing the fasteners. A person who has it works from the alignment data and keeps the sections stress-free while fastening.
skills.learned: On the job after experience in structural assembly.

skills.name: Skin Panel Installation
skills.what: Locating, drilling and fastening skin panels to frames and stringers. A person who has it holds edge margin and contour, deburrs and seals between drilling and fastening.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerostructures plant.

skills.name: Flight Control Surface Installation
skills.what: Hanging rudders, elevators, ailerons, flaps and spoilers on their hinges and connecting their actuators. A person who has it checks hinge alignment, free movement and clearances through full travel.
skills.learned: On the job at an aircraft plant; aviation maintenance schools cover the principles.

skills.name: Flight Control Rigging
skills.what: Adjusting cables, rods and actuators so each control surface is neutral when the control is neutral and moves through its specified travel. A person who has it sets cable tension, installs rig pins and records travel.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; on the job at an aircraft plant.

skills.name: Landing Gear Servicing and Rigging
skills.what: Servicing shock struts with oil and nitrogen, rigging gear doors and uplocks and proving the gear by retraction test on jacks. A person who has it works to the maintenance manual and checks clearances and timing through the full cycle.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; on the job.

skills.name: Hydraulic Line Installation
skills.what: Installing rigid tubes and flexible hoses in a hydraulic system. A person who has it keeps lines clean and capped, routes them without strain or chafing, torques fittings correctly and clamps to spacing.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and fluid power courses; on the job.

skills.name: Closeout Inspection
skills.what: The last look into a bay, tank or compartment before it is closed for good. A person who has it checks for debris, loose hardware, chafing and missing safeties, photographs the area and signs the closeout.
skills.learned: On the job in aircraft and spacecraft assembly, after foreign object and tool control training.

skills.name: Rocket Engine Assembly
skills.what: Building a liquid rocket engine from its major parts: chamber, injector, pumps, valves, ducts and nozzle. A person who has it works to clean-assembly rules, installs seals without damage, torques and safeties every joint and records each step.
skills.learned: On the job at an engine plant, usually from an aircraft engine or precision assembly background.

skills.name: Turbopump Assembly
skills.what: Assembling a rocket engine's pumps: rotor, bearings, seals, inducer and turbine. A person who has it measures and sets axial and radial clearances, balances the rotor and assembles in clean conditions.
skills.learned: On the job at an engine plant, from a turbomachinery or precision assembly background.

skills.name: Propellant Valve Assembly
skills.what: Building and testing valves that control cryogenic and high-pressure propellants. A person who has it installs seats and seals without damage, assembles to cleanliness limits for oxygen service and runs leak and function tests.
skills.learned: On the job at a propulsion or valve plant.

skills.name: Injector Fabrication
skills.what: Making and assembling a rocket engine injector: its orifices, posts and manifolds. A person who has it holds very small hole sizes and positions, keeps passages clean and flow-checks the finished injector.
skills.learned: On the job at a propulsion plant, from precision machining or welding.

skills.name: Regenerative Cooling Channel Fabrication
skills.what: Making the coolant passages in a thrust chamber or nozzle wall, by milling channels and closing them out or by joining tubes. A person who has it holds wall thickness along the channel and proves each passage is open and leak-tight.
skills.learned: On the job at a propulsion plant.

skills.name: Thrust Vector Control Installation
skills.what: Installing the gimbal and actuators that steer a rocket engine and checking their travel. A person who has it sets actuator length and alignment and verifies the engine moves freely through its full range.
skills.learned: On the job at an engine or launch vehicle plant.

skills.name: Thruster Installation
skills.what: Mounting and connecting small spacecraft thrusters: aligning them, connecting propellant lines and electrical leads and leak-checking the joints. A person who has it keeps the propellant system clean and closed throughout.
skills.learned: On the job in spacecraft assembly.
tools: Tube fittings and orbital weld heads

skills.name: Propellant Tank Installation
skills.what: Mounting propellant and pressurant tanks in a vehicle and connecting their lines. A person who has it supports the tank without loading its fittings, torques mounts and proves the joints leak-tight.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch vehicle or spacecraft plant.

skills.name: COPV Installation
skills.what: Installing composite overwrapped pressure vessels that hold high-pressure gas. A person who has it handles them so the overwrap is never struck or scratched, inspects for damage and mounts them without stress.
skills.learned: On the job, with handling and damage-recognition training.

skills.name: Separation System Installation
skills.what: Installing the latches, pushers and release devices that part stages and fairings in flight. A person who has it sets preload and gaps, connects pneumatic or electrical lines and verifies each device is armed as designed.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch vehicle plant.

skills.name: Spacecraft Mechanism Installation
skills.what: Installing and adjusting mechanisms that deploy or move in service: solar arrays, landing legs, hatches, docking hardware and control surfaces. A person who has it sets hinges, latches and actuators and proves the motion in a deployment test.
skills.learned: On the job in spacecraft and launch vehicle assembly.

skills.name: Spacecraft Fluid System Installation
skills.what: Installing life support and thermal control loops: pumps, heat exchangers, tubing and valves. A person who has it keeps the system clean, makes up fittings to torque and proof- and leak-tests the loop.
skills.learned: On the job in spacecraft assembly.
tools: Proof pressure and helium leak test equipment

skills.name: Multi-Layer Insulation Installation
skills.what: Fitting multi-layer insulation blankets to a spacecraft. A person who has it handles the thin layers without tearing or contaminating them, closes seams, grounds each blanket and keeps vents clear.
skills.learned: On the job in spacecraft assembly.

skills.name: Satellite Bus Assembly
skills.what: Building a satellite's structure and installing its units, harness and propulsion, then stacking it for launch. A person who has it works to cleanliness and electrostatic rules and records every fastener and connector mate.
skills.learned: On the job at a satellite plant.

skills.name: Heat Shield Tile Installation
skills.what: Bonding or fastening thermal protection tiles to a vehicle. A person who has it prepares the surface, places each tile to its gap and step limits and proves the bond.
skills.learned: On the job at a spacecraft plant.

skills.name: Parachute Packing
skills.what: Inspecting, folding and packing recovery parachutes to a written procedure with witnessed steps. A person who has it counts every tool and tie, controls line order and records each stage.
skills.learned: On the job under a qualified packer; an FAA parachute rigger certificate is a common background.

skills.name: Missile Assembly
skills.what: Assembling the sections of a guided missile: seeker, guidance, warhead, motor and control surfaces. A person who has it follows explosives safety rules, mates sections and connectors in order and records each step.
skills.learned: On the job at a defense plant, after explosives safety certification.

skills.name: Ballscrew Installation
skills.what: Fitting a ballscrew and its support bearings in a machine axis. A person who has it aligns the screw parallel to the ways, sets bearing preload and checks for binding along the travel.
skills.learned: On the job at a machine tool builder or in machine rebuilding.

skills.name: Linear Guide Installation
skills.what: Mounting linear rails and bearing blocks so an axis runs straight and free. A person who has it sets the master rail to a reference edge, aligns the second rail parallel and tightens in sequence.
skills.learned: On the job at a machine tool or automation equipment builder.

skills.name: Spindle Assembly
skills.what: Building a machine tool spindle: matched bearings, spacers, shaft, drawbar and housing. A person who has it works clean, sets preload, runs the spindle in and checks runout and temperature.
skills.learned: On the job at a spindle or machine tool builder.

skills.name: Hand Scraping of Machine Ways
skills.what: Removing metal by hand from a machine's sliding surfaces until they are flat and bear evenly, with pockets that hold oil. A person who has it reads the blue pattern from a master and scrapes to a set number of contact points.
skills.learned: Long apprenticeship at a machine tool builder or rebuilder.

skills.name: Machine Tool Geometric Alignment
skills.what: Setting a machine tool's axes straight, square and parallel to one another. A person who has it measures with levels, squares and indicators and corrects by shimming, scraping or adjusting.
skills.learned: On the job at a machine tool builder or as a service technician.

skills.name: Machine Leveling
skills.what: Setting a machine level and evenly supported on its foundation. A person who has it adjusts each mount, checks for twist along the bed and rechecks after the machine settles.
skills.learned: Millwright apprenticeship; machine installers learn it on the job.

skills.name: Tube Fitting Make-Up
skills.what: Making up the fittings that join tube in fluid systems: compression, flared and face-seal. A person who has it cuts and deburrs the tube square, bottoms it in the fitting, tightens by turns or to torque, checks the gap and never mixes parts from different makers.
skills.learned: Fitting makers' installer courses, usually a day, and on the job; aviation maintenance schools teach flared fittings.

skills.name: Precision Cleaning
skills.what: Cleaning parts to a verified cleanliness level for oxygen, propellant, vacuum or hydraulic service. A person who has it runs the cleaning steps, verifies by particle count, residue test and black light, and bags and tags the part so it stays clean.
skills.learned: On the job in a clean room or cleaning shop, to the company's specification; ASTM G93 and aerospace oxygen cleaning standards set the levels.
tools: Particle counting and non-volatile residue test kits

skills.name: Proof Pressure and Leak Testing
skills.what: Proving a tube, valve, tank or assembled fluid system holds pressure: a proof test above working pressure, then a leak check. A person who has it sets up the rig behind barriers, raises pressure in steps, holds and reads it, finds leaks with solution, pressure decay or helium and records the result.
skills.learned: On the job, with the employer's pressure systems safety training.
tools: Hydrostatic test pumps and gas boosters

skills.name: Engine Assembly
skills.what: Building an engine from its block or case: crankshaft and bearings, pistons and rods, heads, valve train and timing, each step to torque and angle. A person who has it measures clearances as they build, follows the tightening sequence and turns the engine over by hand before it goes on.
skills.learned: On the job at an engine plant; diesel and automotive technology programs teach the fundamentals.
tools: DC torque tools and angle wrenches

skills.name: Gearbox and Transmission Assembly
skills.what: Assembling gear trains in their housings: shafts, gears, bearings, seals, clutches and shims. A person who has it sets bearing preload and gear backlash by shimming, checks the tooth contact pattern and seals the housing without a leak.
skills.learned: On the job at a transmission, axle or gearbox plant.

skills.name: Body Metal Finishing
skills.what: Finding and removing small dents, dings and high spots in bare body panels before paint. A person who has it finds a defect by hand and with a stone or highlight oil, works it out with pick, hammer and file and leaves a surface that shows nothing under paint.
skills.learned: On the job in a body shop, over years; a recognized skilled classification in automotive plants.

skills.name: Through-Hole Soldering
skills.what: Hand soldering leaded components and wires into plated holes. A person who has it controls tip temperature and time, gets full hole fill and a good fillet, and avoids lifted pads and cold joints.
skills.learned: Electronics programs and employer training; IPC J-STD-001 courses teach and test it.

skills.name: Surface-Mount Soldering
skills.what: Hand soldering and replacing surface-mount parts, from chip resistors to fine-pitch leaded packages. A person who has it works under magnification with paste, flux and hot air without bridging leads or lifting pads.
skills.learned: Electronics programs and employer training; IPC J-STD-001 and IPC-7711/7721 courses.

skills.name: J-STD-001 Soldering
skills.what: Soldering to IPC J-STD-001, the industry requirement for materials, methods and acceptance of soldered connections. A person who has it knows what Class 2 and Class 3 work demands and builds to it.
skills.learned: A J-STD-001 course from an IPC-licensed training center, ending in the Certified IPC Specialist credential, renewed every two years.

skills.name: IPC-A-610 Workmanship Inspection
skills.what: Judging a finished board against IPC-A-610, the acceptance standard for electronic assemblies. A person who has it can tell target, acceptable and defect conditions for solder joints, component placement and damage in each product class.
skills.learned: An IPC-A-610 course from an IPC-licensed training center, ending in the Certified IPC Specialist credential, renewed every two years.

skills.name: Solder Paste Printing
skills.what: Printing solder paste onto a bare board through a stencil. A person who has it aligns the stencil, sets squeegee pressure, speed and separation, manages paste life and cleans the stencil before deposits degrade.
skills.learned: On the job on a surface-mount line; printer makers' training.

skills.name: Solder Paste Inspection Setup
skills.what: Programming and tuning the machine that measures every paste deposit after printing. A person who has it sets volume, height and offset limits tight enough to stop defects without stopping the line for false calls.
skills.learned: On the job on a surface-mount line; machine makers' training.

skills.name: Pick and Place Programming
skills.what: Preparing and tuning a placement machine program: part data, feeder setup, pick positions, vision and placement order. A person who has it loads a new board, corrects mispicks and balances the line for throughput.
skills.learned: On the job as a surface-mount operator moving into setup; machine makers' courses.

skills.name: Reflow Profiling
skills.what: Setting a reflow oven so every joint on a board reaches the right temperature for the right time. A person who has it attaches thermocouples to a board, runs a profile and adjusts zone temperatures and belt speed to meet the paste and component limits.
skills.learned: On the job on a surface-mount line; process engineering courses from equipment and paste suppliers.

skills.name: Wave and Selective Soldering
skills.what: Soldering through-hole parts by passing the board over a wave of molten solder or by a programmed solder nozzle. A person who has it sets flux, preheat, wave height and speed and corrects bridges, skips and poor hole fill.
skills.learned: On the job in an electronics plant; equipment makers' training.

skills.name: Automated Optical Inspection Programming
skills.what: Programming the camera systems that check boards for missing, shifted and wrong parts and bad joints. A person who has it builds the component library, sets thresholds and cuts false calls without letting defects through.
skills.learned: On the job on a surface-mount line; machine makers' training.

skills.name: BGA Rework
skills.what: Removing and replacing ball grid array parts whose joints are hidden under the package. A person who has it profiles the heat for the board, removes the part, dresses the pads and places and reflows the new one.
skills.learned: On the job as an experienced rework technician; IPC-7711/7721 courses cover the methods.
tools: BGA rework stations with split-vision alignment

skills.name: BGA Reballing
skills.what: Putting new solder balls on a removed BGA so it can be used again. A person who has it cleans the old solder, places balls with a stencil or preform and reflows them without damaging the package.
skills.learned: On the job after BGA rework experience.

skills.name: X-Ray Inspection of Solder Joints
skills.what: Using X-ray to see solder joints hidden under BGA, QFN and similar packages. A person who has it finds bridges, opens, head-in-pillow and excess voiding and measures void percentage.
skills.learned: On the job; machine makers' training.

skills.name: PCB Depaneling
skills.what: Separating finished boards from the panel they were built in without cracking parts or joints near the edge. A person who has it sets up the router, saw or laser and fixtures the panel so boards are not flexed.
skills.learned: On the job in an electronics plant.

skills.name: Conformal Coating
skills.what: Applying a thin protective coating over an assembled board. A person who has it masks connectors and keep-out areas, sprays, dips or dispenses to thickness, cures and inspects coverage under UV light.
skills.learned: On the job; coating suppliers' training.
tools: Selective coating machines and spray booths

skills.name: Potting and Encapsulation
skills.what: Filling a housing or covering a circuit with resin to protect it from moisture, vibration and voltage. A person who has it mixes and degasses two-part material, fills without trapping air and cures it.
skills.learned: On the job in electronics and power electronics plants.

skills.name: Component-Level Troubleshooting
skills.what: Finding the failed part on a circuit board from its symptoms and the schematic. A person who has it measures voltages and signals, isolates the fault to a component and replaces it.
skills.learned: Electronics technology associate programs and military electronics training; on the job.

skills.name: Wire Harness Assembly
skills.what: Building a wire harness from a drawing: cutting and marking wire, routing it on a board, terminating, bundling and labeling. A person who has it works to IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship.
skills.learned: On the job; an IPC/WHMA-A-620 course ending in the Certified IPC Specialist credential is the recognized training.

skills.name: Wire Crimping and Termination
