skills.what: Reading piping and instrumentation diagrams. A person who has it follows a process line through its valves, instruments and control loops, and finds each tag in the plant.
skills.learned: Process technology and instrumentation programs; on the job. The symbols follow ISA-5.1.

skills.name: Robot Teach Pendant Operation
skills.what: Running an industrial robot from its pendant: jogging in each coordinate frame, stepping through a program, touching up points and recovering from a fault. A person who has it can get a stopped cell running again safely.
skills.learned: Robotics and mechatronics programs; robot makers' operator courses.

skills.name: Robot Programming
skills.what: Writing and editing programs on an industrial robot, at the teach pendant or in the maker's language: frames, tool and work object data, motion types, registers, I/O, calls and error handling. A person who has it can program a handling, welding or dispensing task from nothing and touch it up on the floor.
skills.learned: Robot makers' programming courses, and their certified training programs at community colleges; robotics and mechatronics programs.

skills.name: Offline Robot Programming and Simulation
skills.what: Programming robots in a 3D model of the cell before it is built. A person who has it checks reach, cycle time and collisions, then downloads and touches up the program on the floor.
skills.learned: Robotics engineering courses; software makers' training.

skills.name: End-of-Arm Tooling Setup
skills.what: Fitting and adjusting what a robot holds: grippers, vacuum cups, weld guns, dispensers and tool changers. A person who has it sets the tool center point and payload, connects air and signals and proves the grip.
skills.learned: Robotics and mechatronics programs; on the job.

skills.name: End-of-Arm Tooling Design
skills.what: Designing the gripper or tool a robot carries for a specific part. A person who has it sizes grip force and vacuum, keeps weight inside the robot's payload and builds in part-present sensing.
skills.learned: Mechanical or mechatronics engineering study; on the job at an integrator.

skills.name: Robot Cell Design
skills.what: Laying out a robot cell: robot choice and reach, fixtures, safeguarding, part flow and cycle time. A person who has it produces a layout that makes rate and passes a risk assessment.
skills.learned: Engineering study; on the job at an integrator or in plant automation.

skills.name: Collaborative Robot Safeguarding
skills.what: Making a collaborative robot application safe to share space with people. A person who has it carries out the risk assessment, sets force and speed limits and safety zones and validates them by measurement. ISO/TS 15066 gives the limits.
skills.learned: Robot makers' and integrators' safety courses.

skills.name: Machine Vision Setup
skills.what: Installing a vision system so it sees the part well: camera and lens choice, working distance, lighting, mounting and calibration. A person who has it gets a sharp, repeatable image before any programming starts.
skills.learned: On the job; vision makers' courses.

skills.name: Machine Vision Programming
skills.what: Programming a vision system to find, measure or inspect a part: pattern matching, edges, blobs, codes and pass/fail logic sent to the controller. A person who has it tunes the tools so good parts pass and bad ones do not.
skills.learned: Vision makers' courses, such as Cognex and Keyence; on the job.
tools: Pattern, edge, blob and code tools

skills.name: Control Panel Building
skills.what: Building an industrial control panel from its drawings: laying out and mounting rail, duct and devices on the back panel, then wiring, ferruling and labeling every conductor. A person who has it wires to the schematic, keeps power and signal apart and checks every point before power is applied.
skills.learned: On the job in a panel shop; electrical programs at community colleges. Panels are built to UL 508A and NFPA 79.
tools: Wire strippers, ferrule crimpers and labelers
Terminal blocks, breakers, contactors and power supplies

skills.name: Robot Mastering and Maintenance
skills.what: Keeping an industrial robot accurate and running: greasing reducers, changing batteries, cables and dress packs, replacing a motor or reducer and re-mastering the axis afterwards. A person who has it backs up the controller first, masters to the witness marks or with the maker's fixture and proves the program points still land.
skills.learned: Robot makers' maintenance courses; robotics and mechatronics programs; on the job.
tools: Grease guns and the maker's greases

skills.name: PID Loop Tuning
skills.what: Setting a control loop's gain, integral and derivative so a temperature, pressure, flow or level reaches its setpoint quickly and stays there. A person who has it bumps the loop, reads the response, tunes it by a method rather than by guess and finds a sticking valve or a noisy sensor before blaming the tuning.
skills.learned: Instrumentation and process control programs; ISA courses; on the job as a controls technician or engineer.
tools: Trend displays and loop tuning software

skills.name: SCADA Development
skills.what: Building the plant-wide system that gathers data from controllers and shows, alarms and stores it: tags, screens, alarm rules, historian and links to databases. A person who has it structures tags and templates so a new machine is added in an hour and keeps alarms few enough to be read.
skills.learned: Automation and controls engineering study; software makers' courses and certifications.

skills.name: Machine Safety Circuit Design
skills.what: Designing and validating the part of a machine's controls that protects people: emergency stops, guard interlocks, light curtains, safety relays and safety controllers. A person who has it works from the risk assessment to the required performance level, designs dual-channel circuits to meet it and proves every safety function before the machine runs.
skills.learned: Controls engineering experience plus machine safety courses and certifications, such as TÜV functional safety for machinery; the standards are ISO 13849, ISO 12100 and NFPA 79.
tools: Light curtains, scanners and interlock switches

skills.name: Preventive Maintenance
skills.what: Carrying out scheduled upkeep on equipment: inspect, clean, lubricate, adjust and replace wear parts before they fail. A person who has it follows the task list, notices what is not on it and records what was found.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs and on the job. The Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals' CMRT is the technician credential.

skills.name: Condition-Based Maintenance
skills.what: Deciding when to service a machine from its measured condition, such as vibration, temperature, oil and motor current, rather than the calendar. A person who has it sets up routes, trends the readings and calls for work when a trend turns.
skills.learned: On the job in a reliability group; vibration and thermography certifications build towards it.

skills.name: Process Equipment Troubleshooting
skills.what: Finding out why a production tool has stopped or is making bad product. A person who has it reads the alarm and the tool's history, checks the likely causes in order and proves the fix before releasing the tool.
skills.learned: On the job, tool by tool; equipment makers' maintenance courses.

skills.name: Equipment Reliability Metrics
skills.what: Working out how reliable equipment is from its history: mean time between failures, mean time to repair and availability. A person who has it cleans the downtime data, calculates the figures and uses them to rank what to fix first.
skills.learned: On the job as an equipment or reliability engineer.

skills.name: Hydraulic System Repair
skills.what: Repairing hydraulic pumps, valves, cylinders and hoses. A person who has it isolates and depressurizes the system, replaces or reseals the component cleanly and bleeds and tests the system afterwards.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs and apprenticeships. The International Fluid Power Society certifies hydraulic mechanics and specialists.

skills.name: Hydraulic System Troubleshooting
skills.what: Finding the cause of a slow, weak, hot or erratic hydraulic system. A person who has it works from the schematic, measuring pressure and flow at test points until the fault is isolated to a component.
skills.learned: Fluid power courses; on the job. The International Fluid Power Society certifies hydraulic specialists.

skills.name: Hydraulic Schematic Reading
skills.what: Reading fluid power diagrams: the symbols for pumps, valves, actuators and accumulators and how a circuit works in each valve position. A person who has it can trace flow and pressure through a machine's circuit.
skills.learned: Fluid power courses in maintenance and mechatronics programs. The symbols follow ISO 1219.

skills.name: Hydraulic Accumulator Service
skills.what: Checking and recharging the nitrogen precharge of an accumulator and replacing its bladder or seals. A person who has it bleeds the oil side to zero first and uses a charging rig, never shop air or oxygen.
skills.learned: Fluid power courses; on the job.

skills.name: Hydraulic Filter Service
skills.what: Changing hydraulic filters and keeping contamination out while the system is open. A person who has it reads the clogging indicator, fits the right element, tops up through a filter and bleeds air.
skills.learned: On the job in maintenance.

skills.name: Hydraulic Fluid Analysis
skills.what: Sampling hydraulic oil and reading the lab report for particles, water and wear metals. A person who has it takes a clean, representative sample and knows the target ISO cleanliness code.
skills.learned: On the job in maintenance or reliability.

skills.name: Hydraulic Pressure and Flow Testing
skills.what: Measuring pressure and flow in a hydraulic system to prove a pump, valve or actuator is doing its job. A person who has it connects test equipment safely and sets relief and reducing valves to specification.
skills.learned: Fluid power courses; on the job.

skills.name: Servo Valve Service
skills.what: Removing, flushing, testing and replacing electrohydraulic servo and proportional valves. A person who has it keeps everything very clean, checks null and response and knows when a valve must go back to the maker.
skills.learned: On the job; valve makers' courses.

skills.name: Pneumatic System Repair
skills.what: Maintaining compressed-air circuits: cylinders, valves, regulators, filters and tubing. A person who has it finds leaks and sticking valves, rebuilds cylinders and sets pressure, speed and cushioning.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance and mechatronics programs. The International Fluid Power Society certifies pneumatic mechanics and specialists.

skills.name: Pump Maintenance
skills.what: Maintaining centrifugal and positive displacement pumps. A person who has it replaces mechanical seals and bearings, sets clearances, aligns the pump to its driver and recognizes cavitation.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance and millwright programs; on the job.

skills.name: Shaft Alignment
skills.what: Aligning the shafts of a motor and the machine it drives so couplings and bearings last. A person who has it corrects soft foot, measures offset and angle and shims and moves the machine into tolerance.
skills.learned: Millwright apprenticeship and industrial maintenance programs; alignment system makers' courses.

skills.name: Gearbox Repair
skills.what: Rebuilding industrial gear reducers. A person who has it strips and inspects gears, bearings and seals, sets backlash and bearing end play, checks the tooth contact pattern and refills with the right oil.
skills.learned: Millwright apprenticeship; on the job.

skills.name: Conveyor Maintenance
skills.what: Keeping conveyors running: tracking and tensioning belts, replacing rollers, bearings, chains and sprockets, and servicing drives. A person who has it tracks a belt that runs off and splices a new one.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs; on the job.

skills.name: Vibration Analysis
skills.what: Measuring a machine's vibration and reading the spectrum to find imbalance, misalignment, looseness and bearing or gear wear. A person who has it collects good data and names the likely fault and its severity.
skills.learned: Certification courses to ISO 18436-2, Categories I to IV, from the Vibration Institute and Mobius Institute.

skills.name: Infrared Thermography
skills.what: Finding faults by their heat with an infrared camera: loose electrical connections, overloaded circuits, failing bearings and insulation gaps. A person who has it sets emissivity and focus, images under load and rates the severity.
skills.learned: Thermographer certification courses, Level I to III, from infrared training providers.

skills.name: Vacuum System Operation
skills.what: Pumping a chamber down and keeping it there. A person who has it knows which pump and gauge work in which pressure range, follows the valve sequence and uses a rate-of-rise test to tell a leak from outgassing.
skills.learned: On the job on vacuum process tools; semiconductor manufacturing programs teach the principles.
tools: Dry and rotary vane roughing pumps

skills.name: Helium Leak Detection
skills.what: Finding leaks in vacuum and pressure systems with a helium mass spectrometer. A person who has it calibrates the detector, sprays or sniffs joints in a sensible order and tells a real leak from background.
skills.learned: On the job; leak detector makers' courses.

skills.name: Residual Gas Analysis
skills.what: Reading the mass spectrum of the gas left in a vacuum chamber. A person who has it tells an air leak from water or contamination by the peaks present and tracks chamber condition over time.
skills.learned: On the job as a vacuum or equipment engineer.
tools: Quadrupole residual gas analyzers and their software

skills.name: Ultrapure Water System Operation
skills.what: Running the plant that makes ultrapure water for a fab. A person who has it monitors resistivity, organic carbon, particles and flow through each stage and changes filters and resins on condition.
skills.learned: On the job in fab facilities, often from a water treatment background.

skills.name: Aircraft Maintenance Manual Use
skills.what: Finding and following the current, approved maintenance data for a task: the maintenance manual, parts catalog, wiring manual and service bulletins. A person who has it confirms the data applies to the specific aircraft before starting.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training.

skills.name: Aircraft Maintenance Record Entries
skills.what: Recording maintenance as 14 CFR Part 43 requires: what was done, with what data, when, and by whom, with signature and certificate number. A person who has it writes entries that support return to service.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; the certificate itself is the authority to sign.

skills.name: Aircraft Engine Ground Run
skills.what: Starting and running an aircraft's engines on the ground for leak, function and performance checks. A person who has it follows the checklist, watches limits and knows the emergency shutdown actions.
skills.learned: Employer run-and-taxi qualification on the aircraft type, held in addition to an FAA Airframe and Powerplant certificate.

skills.name: Aircraft Wheel and Tire Service
skills.what: Removing, inspecting, building up and installing aircraft wheels and tires. A person who has it deflates before disassembly, inflates in a safety cage with nitrogen and checks brake wear.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; on the job.

skills.name: Aircraft Sheet Metal Repair
skills.what: Repairing damaged aircraft skin and structure with patches, doublers and splices. A person who has it removes rivets without enlarging holes, lays out a rivet pattern with correct edge distance and spacing and restores the original strength.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; repairs follow the structural repair manual or FAA Advisory Circular 43.13-1B.

skills.name: Aircraft Corrosion Control
skills.what: Finding, removing and treating corrosion on aircraft structure. A person who has it identifies the type, blends it out within limits, restores the conversion coat and primer and applies preventive compound.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training.

skills.name: Aircraft Bleed Air System Service
skills.what: Inspecting, leak-checking and replacing the ducts, valves and clamps that carry hot engine bleed air. A person who has it finds leaks, tests valves and installs duct joints so they stay sealed.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; on the job.

skills.name: Rocket Engine Refurbishment
skills.what: Bringing a flown rocket engine back to flight condition: inspecting it, cleaning it and replacing seals and worn parts. A person who has it works to the reuse limits for each part and records what was found.
skills.learned: On the job at an engine plant, after engine assembly experience.

skills.name: Post-Flight Hardware Inspection
skills.what: Inspecting flown hardware for heat damage, cracks, leaks and wear before it flies again. A person who has it follows the inspection plan, documents each finding and knows what needs engineering review.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch vehicle plant, from an aircraft or structures inspection background.

skills.name: Transporter-Erector Operation
skills.what: Operating the heavy hydraulic equipment that carries a rocket to the pad and raises it upright. A person who has it runs the lift sequence, watches loads and pressures and services the hydraulics.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch site, from a heavy equipment or hydraulics background.

skills.name: Umbilical Connection and Checkout
skills.what: Connecting and checking the ground lines that feed a vehicle fluids, gases, power and data until liftoff. A person who has it mates each connection, leak-checks it and verifies the release mechanism.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch or test site.

skills.name: Quick-Disconnect Coupling Service
skills.what: Inspecting, mating and maintaining quick-disconnect couplings on propellant and gas lines. A person who has it checks seals, engages and locks the coupling and proves it leak-tight.
skills.learned: On the job in ground support or test.

skills.name: CMMS Use
skills.what: Working in a plant's maintenance management system: opening and closing work orders, recording what was found and done, booking parts and labor and looking up an asset's history. A person who has it leaves a record the next technician can use.
skills.learned: On the job on the plant's system.

skills.name: Machine Lubrication
skills.what: Keeping machines lubricated: the right oil or grease, in the right amount, at the right interval, kept clean on the way in. A person who has it follows the lubrication route, reads sight glasses and reservoirs, greases a bearing without blowing its seal and takes a clean oil sample.
skills.learned: On the job as a maintenance helper or oiler; the Society of Tribologists and Lubrication Engineers and ICML certify lubrication technicians.

skills.name: Belt and Chain Drive Maintenance
skills.what: Installing and maintaining belt and chain drives: aligning sheaves and sprockets, setting tension and replacing worn belts, chains and sprockets. A person who has it reads a wear pattern for its cause and sets tension by measurement, not by feel.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs and millwright apprenticeships; on the job.

skills.name: Laser Optics Maintenance
skills.what: Keeping an industrial laser's beam path in condition: inspecting and changing cover slides, lenses and mirrors, aligning the beam to the nozzle or scanner and checking power at the work. A person who has it handles optics without marking them, aligns under the laser safety rules and finds whether a weak cut or weld is the source, the fiber or the head.
skills.learned: Laser makers' service courses after laser safety training; on the job as a laser technician.
tools: Fiber, disk and CO2 laser sources

skills.name: Compressed Air System Maintenance
skills.what: Keeping a plant's compressed air running: servicing compressors, dryers, filters, drains and receivers and finding leaks in the distribution. A person who has it changes separators and filters on hours, checks dew point and pressure drop and reads a compressor's controller for the cause of a trip.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs; compressor makers' service courses; on the job.

skills.name: Chiller and HVAC Maintenance
skills.what: Maintaining the chillers, cooling towers, air handlers and process cooling loops a plant depends on. A person who has it checks refrigerant pressures and temperatures, cleans coils and strainers, treats and tests the water and changes filters and belts; opening a refrigerant circuit needs EPA Section 608 certification.
skills.learned: HVAC and refrigeration programs at community colleges; EPA Section 608 certification; on the job.

skills.name: Caliper Measurement
skills.what: Measuring outside, inside, depth and step dimensions with dial or digital calipers to about a thousandth of an inch. A person who has it zeroes the tool, holds it square with light, even pressure and knows when a caliper is not accurate enough.
skills.learned: Taught in the first weeks of machining and quality programs; NIMS Measurement, Materials and Safety credential.

skills.name: Micrometer Measurement
skills.what: Measuring to a ten-thousandth of an inch with outside, inside and depth micrometers. A person who has it reads the thimble and vernier, uses the ratchet for consistent feel and checks zero against a standard.
skills.learned: Machining and quality programs; NIMS Measurement, Materials and Safety credential.

skills.name: Height Gauge Measurement
skills.what: Measuring heights, steps and hole locations from a surface plate. A person who has it sets the part on its datum, zeroes the gauge and uses an indicator or probe to pick up each feature.
skills.learned: Machining and quality programs; on the job in inspection.

skills.name: Bore Gauge Measurement
skills.what: Measuring inside diameters to tenths with a dial bore gauge. A person who has it sets the gauge to a master, rocks it to find the true reading and checks a bore for taper and out-of-round.
skills.learned: Machining and quality programs; on the job.

skills.name: Gauge Block Use
skills.what: Building an exact length by wringing gauge blocks together, to set or check other instruments. A person who has it picks the fewest blocks, wrings them clean and handles them so they neither warm nor rust.
skills.learned: Metrology and toolmaking courses; on the job in a calibration lab.
tools: Steel and ceramic gauge block sets

skills.name: Thread Measurement
skills.what: Checking screw threads for size and form. A person who has it uses go and no-go gauges correctly and measures pitch diameter with thread micrometers or the three-wire method.
skills.learned: Machining and inspection programs; on the job.

skills.name: Surface Roughness Measurement
skills.what: Measuring surface finish with a stylus profilometer and reading values such as Ra and Rz against the drawing. A person who has it sets cutoff and trace direction correctly and checks the instrument on a reference specimen.
skills.learned: Machining and quality programs; on the job.

skills.name: Optical Comparator Inspection
skills.what: Inspecting a part's profile as a magnified shadow on a screen. A person who has it stages and aligns the part, picks the magnification and measures with the stage, an overlay or edge detection.
skills.learned: Quality and machining programs; on the job in inspection.

skills.name: GD&T Interpretation
skills.what: Reading geometric dimensioning and tolerancing on a drawing: datums, feature control frames, material condition modifiers and each of the tolerance symbols. A person who has it knows what a callout allows and how the feature must be set up and measured.
skills.learned: Courses at community colleges and from training firms. ASME certifies Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing Professionals at Technologist and Senior levels, to its Y14.5 standard.

skills.name: Tolerance Stack-Up Analysis
skills.what: Adding up the tolerances along a chain of parts to find the largest and smallest gap or interference an assembly can have. A person who has it runs worst-case and statistical stacks and says which tolerance to change.
skills.learned: Mechanical engineering study and GD&T courses; on the job in design.

skills.name: CMM Operation
skills.what: Running a coordinate measuring machine: fixturing the part, qualifying probes, running a program and reading the report. A person who has it knows when a result is wrong because of the setup, not the part.
skills.learned: Quality programs at community colleges; CMM makers' operator courses; on the job.

skills.name: CMM Programming
skills.what: Writing the measurement program for a part from its drawing and model. A person who has it builds the alignment from the datums, chooses how many points to take on each feature, sets probe angles and outputs the dimensions the drawing requires.
skills.learned: CMM makers' programming courses after operating experience.

skills.name: CMM Part Alignment
skills.what: Establishing a part's coordinate system on a measuring machine from its datum features, or by best fit to the model. A person who has it gets the same alignment the drawing intends, which every reported dimension depends on.
skills.learned: CMM makers' advanced courses; on the job as a senior programmer or metrologist.

skills.name: Laser Tracker Metrology
skills.what: Measuring large parts, tools and assemblies with a laser tracker and a hand-held reflector. A person who has it locates the tracker, ties in to reference points and reports positions against the model.
skills.learned: Tracker makers' courses; the Coordinate Metrology Society certifies portable metrology operators.

skills.name: 3D Scanning
skills.what: Capturing a part's whole surface with a structured-light or laser scanner. A person who has it prepares the surface, plans the scan positions and gets complete, accurate data.
skills.learned: Scanner makers' courses; on the job in a metrology lab.
tools: Laser line scanners and scanning arms

skills.name: Scan Data Processing
skills.what: Turning scan or CT data into results: cleaning and aligning the point cloud, comparing it with the CAD model as a color map and extracting dimensions. A person who has it knows how alignment choices change the answer.
skills.learned: Software makers' courses; on the job in metrology.

skills.name: Body Dimensional Measurement
skills.what: Measuring a vehicle body or its subassemblies against the model, at the points that control fit. A person who has it sets the body on its locators, measures by CMM or optical system and reports deviations by zone.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive body shop or metrology lab.

skills.name: Ballbar Testing
skills.what: Checking how well a CNC machine moves in a circle, using a telescoping bar between spindle and table. A person who has it runs the test and reads the plot for backlash, squareness, scale and servo mismatch.
skills.learned: On the job as a machine tool service or maintenance technician; ballbar makers' training.

skills.name: Machine Tool Laser Calibration
skills.what: Measuring how accurately a machine axis positions along its travel with a laser interferometer. A person who has it aligns the optics, records the errors and reports accuracy and repeatability.
skills.learned: On the job as a machine tool service technician; interferometer makers' training.
tools: Laser interferometer systems such as Renishaw XL-80

skills.name: CNC Axis Error Compensation
skills.what: Entering measured errors into a CNC control so the machine corrects itself: pitch error tables, backlash and squareness values. A person who has it loads the compensation and verifies the gain with a second measurement.
skills.learned: On the job as a machine tool service technician.

skills.name: Pressure Gauge Calibration
skills.what: Comparing a pressure gauge or transmitter with a more accurate standard across its range. A person who has it applies pressure in steps, up and down, records the errors and adjusts or rejects the instrument.
skills.learned: Metrology and instrumentation programs; on the job in a calibration lab. ASQ offers the Certified Calibration Technician credential.

skills.name: Temperature Calibration
skills.what: Comparing thermocouples, resistance thermometers and indicators with a reference at set temperatures. A person who has it gives each point time to settle, records the error and applies or reports corrections.
skills.learned: Metrology and instrumentation programs; on the job. ASQ offers the Certified Calibration Technician credential.

skills.name: Torque Wrench Calibration
skills.what: Checking a torque tool against a transducer at points across its range. A person who has it loads the wrench correctly, records the readings, adjusts it and labels it with the due date.
skills.learned: On the job in a calibration lab or tool crib. ASQ offers the Certified Calibration Technician credential.

skills.name: Measurement Uncertainty Analysis
skills.what: Estimating how far a measurement could be from the true value. A person who has it lists the contributors, such as the standard, resolution, repeatability and temperature, combines them in a budget and states the expanded uncertainty.
skills.learned: Metrology courses; on the job in a calibration lab accredited to ISO/IEC 17025. ASQ's Certified Calibration Technician covers the basics.

skills.name: In-Process Inspection
skills.what: Checking parts at the machine or station while the job runs, at the frequency the control plan sets. A person who has it measures the called-out features, records them and stops the job when a trend or a part goes out.
skills.learned: On the job; machining and quality programs.

skills.name: First Article Inspection
skills.what: Verifying every dimension, note and requirement on the first part from a new or changed process. A person who has it balloons the drawing, measures each characteristic and completes the report, in aerospace on the three forms of AS9102.
skills.learned: On the job in inspection; quality programs.

skills.name: Inspection Record Keeping
skills.what: Recording inspection results so they can be trusted later: actual values, the gauge used, date, stamp or signature, and corrections made properly. A person who has it leaves a record that stands up in an audit.
skills.learned: On the job; covered in quality programs.

skills.name: Nonconformance Reporting
skills.what: Writing up a part that does not meet requirements: what the requirement is, what was found, how many, and where the parts are held. A person who has it tags and segregates the material and writes a report someone else can act on.
skills.learned: On the job in inspection; quality programs.

skills.name: Material Review Board Disposition
skills.what: Deciding what happens to nonconforming material: use as is, rework, repair, return or scrap. A person who has it presents the facts, knows who has authority for each disposition and records the decision.
skills.learned: On the job in quality or manufacturing engineering.

skills.name: Acceptance Sampling
skills.what: Inspecting a sample from a lot and accepting or rejecting the lot on the result. A person who has it reads sample size and accept number from the plan for the lot size and quality level, and picks the sample at random.
skills.learned: Quality programs; covered by ASQ's Certified Quality Inspector and Technician credentials. The common plans are ANSI/ASQ Z1.4.

skills.name: Material Traceability Records
skills.what: Keeping the chain of paperwork that ties a part to its material, processes and inspections: mill certificates, lot numbers, process certifications and serial numbers. A person who has it can prove where a part came from.
skills.learned: On the job in receiving, stores and inspection.

skills.name: Statistical Process Control
skills.what: Charting measurements from a process to tell normal variation from a real change. A person who has it plots the data, recognizes out-of-control signals and reacts as the control plan says.
skills.learned: Quality programs; employer training. Covered by ASQ's Certified Quality Technician and Engineer credentials.
tools: X-bar and R, individuals and attribute charts

skills.name: Process Capability Analysis
skills.what: Comparing a process's spread and centering with the tolerance, as Cp and Cpk. A person who has it collects enough stable data, checks its distribution and says whether the process can hold the tolerance.
skills.learned: Quality and engineering programs; ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer and Six Sigma credentials.

skills.name: Gauge R&R Studies
skills.what: Testing a measurement system by having several people measure the same parts several times, to split gauge variation into repeatability and reproducibility. A person who has it runs the study and judges whether the gauge is fit for the tolerance.
skills.learned: Quality programs; AIAG's Measurement Systems Analysis manual is the reference.

skills.name: Design of Experiments
skills.what: Changing several process settings together in a planned pattern to learn which matter and how they interact. A person who has it picks factors and levels, runs the trials in random order and reads the effects.
skills.learned: Engineering study; ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer and Six Sigma Black Belt credentials.

skills.name: Root Cause Analysis
skills.what: Working from a failure back to the cause that, once removed, stops it happening again. A person who has it gathers the facts first, uses five-whys and cause-and-effect diagrams and tests the suspected cause before closing.
skills.learned: Employer training; quality programs. Covered by ASQ's quality credentials.

skills.name: 8D Problem Solving
skills.what: Solving a customer problem in the eight disciplines: team, problem description, containment, root cause, corrective action, verification, prevention and closure. A person who has it writes an 8D report the customer accepts.
skills.learned: Employer and customer training in automotive and electronics supply chains.

skills.name: Corrective and Preventive Action
skills.what: Running a corrective action from the problem to proof that it worked: investigation, root cause, action, verification of effectiveness. A person who has it writes records that satisfy the quality system and its auditors.
skills.learned: On the job in quality; ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer and Auditor credentials cover it.

skills.name: Process FMEA
skills.what: Listing the ways each process step can fail, what each failure does and how it is caught, then ranking them to decide what to fix first. A person who has it builds the analysis with the people who run the process and keeps it current.
skills.learned: Employer training; AIAG's FMEA handbook is the reference. Covered by ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer.

skills.name: Design FMEA
skills.what: Listing the ways a design can fail to do its job, the effects and the causes, and ranking them to decide what to change or test. A person who has it ties each failure mode to a design control.
skills.learned: Engineering study and employer training; AIAG's FMEA handbook is the reference.

skills.name: Control Plan Development
skills.what: Writing the control plan: for each process step, what is checked, how, how often, by whom and what to do when it fails. A person who has it links the plan to the FMEA and the drawing's key characteristics.
skills.learned: Employer training in automotive and aerospace quality; AIAG's APQP manual is the reference.

skills.name: PPAP Submission
skills.what: Assembling the evidence that a supplier's process can make a part to requirements: dimensional results, material and performance tests, capability studies, control plan and the signed warrant. A person who has it prepares or reviews a complete package.
skills.learned: Employer training in the automotive supply chain; AIAG's PPAP manual is the reference.

skills.name: Quality System Auditing
skills.what: Auditing a plant's quality management system against its standard: ISO 9001, and in aerospace AS9100, in automotive IATF 16949, in medical devices ISO 13485. A person who has it plans the audit, follows a process from requirement to record, writes findings on evidence and checks that the corrective action worked; they can also prepare their own area to be audited.
skills.learned: Internal auditor and lead auditor courses for the standard; ASQ's Certified Quality Auditor credential.
tools: The standard and the quality manual

skills.name: Work Instruction Writing
skills.what: Writing instructions an operator can follow without asking: one action per step, in order, with photos, torque values, tools and checks. A person who has it tries the instruction on the floor and controls its revisions.
skills.learned: On the job in manufacturing engineering.
tools: Work instruction templates and authoring software

skills.name: 5S Workplace Organization
skills.what: Organizing a work area by sort, set in order, shine, standardize and sustain, so everything needed has a marked place and anything abnormal shows. A person who has it sets up an area and keeps it audited.
skills.learned: Employer training; lean certificate programs.

skills.name: Standard Work
skills.what: Documenting the best known way to do a job, with its sequence, timing against takt and the work in process allowed, and working to it. A person who has it writes the standard work sheets and improves them with the operators.
skills.learned: Employer lean training; SME's Lean Certification covers it.

skills.name: Value Stream Mapping
skills.what: Drawing how material and information flow for a product family, from order to shipment, to see where time is lost. A person who has it maps the current state on the floor, measures lead time against work time and draws a future state.
skills.learned: Employer lean training; SME's Lean Certification covers it.

skills.name: Kaizen Event Facilitation
skills.what: Leading a short, focused improvement event in which a team studies an area, changes it and proves the result within days. A person who has it scopes the event, keeps the team on the method and follows up on open actions.
skills.learned: Employer lean training; SME's Lean Certification covers it.

skills.name: Six Sigma DMAIC
skills.what: Running an improvement project through define, measure, analyze, improve and control, using data at each step. A person who has it scopes a project, validates the measurement, finds the significant causes and holds the gain.
skills.learned: ASQ's Certified Six Sigma Green Belt and Black Belt, or an employer's belt program.

skills.name: Quick Changeover
skills.what: Cutting the time a machine is down between jobs. A person who has it films a changeover, separates what can be done while the machine runs from what cannot, and standardizes tools, positions and clamping.
skills.learned: Employer lean training; on the job in setup.

skills.name: Line Balancing
skills.what: Dividing the work of an assembly line among stations so each fits within takt time. A person who has it lists the work elements and their times, respects the order they must follow and levels the load.
skills.learned: Industrial engineering study; on the job.

skills.name: Time Study
skills.what: Measuring how long a job takes: breaking it into elements, timing them over many cycles and applying allowances to set a standard time. A person who has it gets a figure both operators and planners accept.
skills.learned: Industrial engineering study; on the job.

skills.name: Error Proofing
skills.what: Designing a process so a mistake cannot be made or is caught at once: pins that stop a part going in backwards, sensors that confirm a part is present, tools that count. A person who has it finds where errors happen and adds the simplest device that stops them.
skills.learned: Employer lean and quality training; on the job in manufacturing engineering.

skills.name: OEE Analysis
skills.what: Measuring how much of a machine's scheduled time makes good parts at full speed, as availability, performance and quality. A person who has it collects honest loss data and ranks the losses.
skills.learned: Employer training; on the job in industrial engineering and maintenance.

skills.name: Metallographic Examination
skills.what: Preparing and examining a metal sample under the microscope: section, mount, grind, polish and etch. A person who has it reads grain structure, case depth, weld penetration and porosity and takes microhardness traverses.
skills.learned: Materials science and metallurgical technology programs; on the job in a materials lab.

skills.name: Tensile Testing
skills.what: Pulling a specimen to failure to measure its yield strength, tensile strength and elongation. A person who has it prepares and measures the specimen, sets up grips and extensometer and reports the results. The method for metals is ASTM E8.
skills.learned: Materials and engineering technology programs; on the job in a materials lab.

skills.name: Vehicle Final Inspection
skills.what: Checking a finished vehicle before it leaves the line: fit and finish, function of every feature, fluid leaks and stored fault codes. A person who has it follows the inspection route, records each defect and confirms its repair.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Thermal Protection System Inspection
skills.what: Inspecting a vehicle's heat shield: tile gaps and steps, bond condition, cracks and chips. A person who has it measures to the limits and marks anything that needs repair.
skills.learned: On the job at a spacecraft plant.

skills.name: Dial Indicator Measurement
skills.what: Measuring small movements and differences with a dial or test indicator: runout, flatness, parallelism and position against a reference. A person who has it mounts the indicator rigidly, sets the contact angle, preloads and zeroes it and reads total indicator movement.
skills.learned: Taught in the first term of machining and quality programs; on the job.

skills.name: Pin and Plug Gauge Use
skills.what: Checking holes, slots and diameters with fixed gauges: pin gauges, go and no-go plugs, rings and snap gauges. A person who has it picks the gauge from the tolerance, uses a light, straight feel without forcing and looks after gauges so they stay to size.
skills.learned: Taught in the first weeks on a machine or inspection bench; machining and quality programs.

skills.name: Surface Plate Inspection
skills.what: Setting a part up on a granite surface plate to measure it from its datums, with angle plates, V-blocks, parallels, a sine bar and an indicator. A person who has it builds the setup the drawing's datums call for and works out an angle or a position from gauge blocks and indicator readings.
skills.learned: Quality and machining programs; on the job in an inspection room.

skills.name: Dimensional Gauge Calibration
skills.what: Calibrating the gauges a shop measures with: calipers, micrometers, indicators, height gauges, pins, plugs and thread gauges. A person who has it lets gauge and standard reach the same temperature, checks across the range against gauge blocks or masters, adjusts or rejects and records as-found and as-left values.
skills.learned: On the job in a calibration laboratory; military metrology schools; ASQ's Certified Calibration Technician credential.
tools: Bench micrometers and universal length machines

skills.name: Electrical Instrument Calibration
skills.what: Calibrating electrical test equipment: multimeters, power supplies, oscilloscopes, insulation testers and clamp meters. A person who has it applies known values from a calibrator at the points the procedure lists, compares readings with tolerance and records as-found and as-left values.
skills.learned: Military metrology schools and electronics programs; on the job in a calibration laboratory. ASQ's Certified Calibration Technician credential.

skills.name: Visual Testing
skills.what: Examining a surface directly by eye, with adequate light and simple aids, for cracks, corrosion, damage and workmanship defects. A person who has it knows the acceptance criteria and inspects at the required distance, angle and light level.
skills.learned: Employer training and certification under SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410; the first method most inspectors learn.

skills.name: Borescope Inspection
skills.what: Looking inside engines, tanks, tubes and closed structure with a borescope. A person who has it guides the probe without damaging anything, recognizes cracks, burns, erosion and debris and measures and records what is found.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training and engine makers' courses; on the job.

skills.name: Liquid Penetrant Testing
skills.what: Finding cracks and porosity open to the surface: clean the part, apply penetrant, let it dwell, remove the excess, apply developer and read the indications. A person who has it carries out each step to the procedure, with spray cans and wiping in the field or on a process line, applies a thin, even developer and tells a relevant indication from a false one.
skills.learned: Classroom hours and supervised experience leading to Level II certification by the employer, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A or, in aerospace, NAS 410.

skills.name: Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection
skills.what: Penetrant testing with a dye that glows under UV-A light in a darkened booth, the more sensitive form used on aerospace parts, run on a line as water-washable or post-emulsifiable penetrant at the sensitivity level the part requires. A person who has it controls wash pressure, temperature and time, or emulsifier contact time and concentration, so penetrant is not washed out of a defect, then adapts their eyes and inspects every surface. ASTM E1417 sets the process.
skills.learned: Level II penetrant certification under NAS 410, with experience on a fluorescent line.

skills.name: Penetrant System Performance Checks
skills.what: Proving a penetrant line still works: running a known-defect panel each day, measuring UV-A intensity at the part and white light in the booth, and checking penetrant, emulsifier, developer, wash and dryer on schedule. A person who has it runs the checks, keeps the log and takes a lamp or a bath out of use when it falls short.
skills.learned: On the job on a penetrant line, as part of Level II certification; the light checks are shared with fluorescent magnetic particle inspection.
tools: UV-A radiometers and white light meters

skills.name: Magnetic Particle Testing
skills.what: Finding surface and near-surface cracks in steel by magnetizing it and applying iron particles, which gather at a flaw. A person who has it magnetizes in two directions at right angles, with a yoke and dry powder on welds and castings or on a bench, applies particles while the field is on, interprets the indications and demagnetizes the part afterwards.
skills.learned: Classroom hours and supervised experience leading to Level II certification by the employer, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410.
tools: AC and DC yokes and lift test weights

skills.name: Wet Fluorescent Magnetic Particle Inspection
skills.what: Magnetic particle testing on a wet bench with fluorescent particles in a liquid bath, read under UV-A light: a head shot or central conductor for flaws that run lengthwise, a coil for flaws that run around the part. A person who has it sets current for the part's diameter and length, makes good contact to avoid arc burns, checks bath concentration by settling test and inspects in a darkened booth. ASTM E1444 sets the process.
skills.learned: Level II magnetic particle certification, with experience on a wet bench.
tools: Contact pads and central conductor bars

skills.name: MT Field Strength Measurement
skills.what: Choosing the magnetizing current for a part and proving the field it gives: alternating for surface cracks, half-wave or full-wave direct for flaws a little below the surface, at an amperage that shows a known flaw. A person who has it uses notched shims, pie gauges and a gauss meter and adjusts the setup until the field is adequate in strength and direction.
skills.learned: Learned as part of Level II magnetic particle certification; setting the technique for a new part is Level III work.

skills.name: Ultrasonic Testing
skills.what: Finding internal flaws by sending high-frequency sound into a part and reading the echoes on the A-scan, where echo height is plotted against time. A person who has it sets up and calibrates the instrument, scans by hand with consistent coupling and overlap, tells back wall, geometry and flaw echoes apart, watches for loss of back wall and evaluates indications to the procedure.
skills.learned: Classroom hours and supervised experience leading to Level II certification by the employer, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410.

skills.name: UT Calibration with Reference Blocks
skills.what: Choosing the transducer for an inspection and setting the instrument up on standard blocks before it: frequency, size and angle, then range, sensitivity, beam exit point and angle. A person who has it trades penetration against sensitivity, calibrates on the right block for the job and rechecks during and after the inspection.
skills.learned: Learned as part of Level I and II ultrasonic certification.
tools: Contact, angle-beam, dual-element and delay-line transducers

skills.name: Angle-Beam UT
skills.what: Inspecting with sound sent in at an angle, as shear waves, to reach flaws in welds and around geometry: lack of fusion, cracks, slag and porosity. A person who has it plots the sound path, scans a weld from both sides, locates each reflector in the cross-section from its surface distance and depth and accepts or rejects it to the code.
skills.learned: Level II ultrasonic certification with weld experience; AWS D1.1 and ASME Section V set the methods.

skills.name: Immersion UT
skills.what: Inspecting a part under water, or between water jets, with the transducer held off the surface by a scanner that maps the result as a C-scan. A person who has it sets water path and angle, normalizes the probe to the surface, keeps a sender and receiver aligned for through-transmission, sets the gates and marks out and measures each indication on the map.
skills.learned: Level II ultrasonic certification, with experience on an immersion system.

skills.name: UT Thickness Measurement
skills.what: Measuring wall thickness from one side with ultrasound, to find thinning from corrosion or machining. A person who has it calibrates on a step block of the same material and corrects for temperature and coatings.
skills.learned: Short employer courses; part of Level I and II ultrasonic certification.

skills.name: UT Flaw Sizing
skills.what: Judging how large a reflector is from its echo. A person who has it builds a distance-amplitude curve from reference reflectors, compares indications against it and measures length by probe movement.
skills.learned: Learned as part of Level II ultrasonic certification.
tools: Reference blocks with side-drilled and flat-bottom holes
Flaw detectors with DAC and TCG functions

skills.name: UT of Composites
skills.what: Ultrasonic inspection of composite laminates and bonded structure for delaminations, disbonds, porosity and inclusions. A person who has it calibrates on a reference panel of the same layup, reads signal loss as well as echoes and estimates porosity from attenuation against reference panels.
skills.learned: Level II ultrasonic certification with composite experience, under NAS 410.

skills.name: Phased Array UT
was: Phased Array Data Acquisition and Analysis
skills.what: Ultrasonic testing with a multi-element probe whose beam is steered and focused electronically, recorded with an encoder and analyzed afterwards. A person who has it sets up linear and sectorial scans and the scan plan, calibrates each beam, checks data quality and sizes indications from the stored views; full matrix capture with the total focusing method is the same work with a reconstructed image.
skills.learned: A phased array course and supervised hours on top of Level II ultrasonic certification.

skills.name: Time-of-Flight Diffraction
skills.what: Sizing weld flaws from the faint signals diffracted by their tips, using a sender and receiver on either side of the weld. A person who has it sets probe separation and reads through-wall height from the image.
skills.learned: A specialist course and supervised hours on top of Level II ultrasonic certification.

skills.name: Radiographic Testing
skills.what: Finding internal flaws by passing X-rays or gamma rays through a part onto film or a detector. A person who has it works out the exposure from material and thickness, places source, film, markers and the image quality indicator, controls scatter with collimators, masks and lead backing and produces an image of the required density and sensitivity.
skills.learned: Classroom hours and supervised experience leading to Level II certification by the employer, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410, plus radiation safety training.
tools: Exposure charts and source decay tables

skills.name: Radiographic Film Processing
skills.what: Developing exposed film by hand or in a processor. A person who has it controls developer temperature, time and replenishment, avoids marks and fog and checks density with a densitometer.
skills.learned: Learned as part of Level I and II radiographic certification.

skills.name: Digital Radiography
skills.what: Radiography without film: a flat-panel detector that shows the image at once, or a reusable phosphor plate read by a laser scanner. A person who has it calibrates the detector or sets exposure for the plate, sets geometry and checks sharpness and contrast on screen against the requirement.
skills.learned: Level II radiographic certification with digital training.

skills.name: Radiograph Interpretation
skills.what: Reading a radiograph: first confirming its quality, then finding and naming each indication and judging it against the acceptance standard, the code for a weld or the reference radiographs for a casting. A person who has it tells porosity, inclusions, shrinkage, cracks and lack of fusion from film artifacts.
skills.learned: Level II radiographic certification, with many hours of supervised film reading. ASME Section V and AWS D1.1 govern welds; ASTM publishes reference radiographs for castings, such as E155 for aluminum and E446 for steel.

skills.name: Real-Time X-Ray Inspection of Castings
skills.what: Checking production castings for porosity and inclusions on an X-ray cell that shows the image live. A person who has it runs the cell, compares what it sees with the acceptance level for each zone and sorts the castings.
skills.learned: On the job at a casting plant, with radiation safety training.

skills.name: Industrial CT Scanning
skills.what: Building a 3D picture of a part's inside from many X-ray views. A person who has it fixtures the part, sets voltage, filtering and resolution, reconstructs the volume and inspects it for porosity, cracks and dimensions.
skills.learned: On the job in a CT lab, with radiation safety training; system makers' courses.

skills.name: Eddy Current Testing
skills.what: Finding surface cracks in metal with a probe that induces eddy currents and senses how a flaw disturbs them. A person who has it picks probe and frequency for the material and depth, sets up on a notched reference standard, sets gain and rotation so a crack signal stands apart from lift-off and geometry on the impedance plane, and scans edges, radii and fastener rows.
skills.learned: Classroom hours and supervised experience leading to Level II certification by the employer, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410.
tools: Pencil, spot, ring and sliding probes

skills.name: Bolt Hole Eddy Current Inspection
skills.what: Inspecting the bore of a fastener hole for cracks with a rotating probe. A person who has it picks the probe for the hole size, sets up on a notched standard and indexes through the full depth.
skills.learned: Level II eddy current certification with aircraft structure experience.

skills.name: Eddy Current Array Inspection
skills.what: Scanning a wide strip in one pass with a probe that holds many coils, giving a mapped image. A person who has it sets up the array, encodes the scan and reads the color map.
skills.learned: Advanced course after Level II eddy current certification.

skills.name: Eddy Current Conductivity Measurement
skills.what: Measuring electrical conductivity with an eddy current meter to verify an aluminum alloy's temper or find heat damage. A person who has it calibrates on standards near the expected value and corrects for temperature.
skills.learned: Short employer courses; part of Level I and II eddy current certification.

skills.name: Eddy Current Inspection of Aircraft Structure
skills.what: Eddy current inspection of aircraft structure: cracks at fasteners and radii, and corrosion or cracks in a second layer found at low frequency. A person who has it works to the aircraft's non-destructive testing manual.
skills.learned: Level II eddy current certification under NAS 410 with aircraft experience.

skills.name: NDT Procedure Writing
skills.what: Writing the procedure an inspection is carried out to: equipment, calibration, coverage, sensitivity and acceptance criteria. A person who has it turns a code or customer requirement into steps a Level II can follow, and qualifies the technique.
skills.learned: Level III certification in the method; on the job.

skills.name: NDT Reference Standard Design
skills.what: Specifying and verifying the reference standards an inspection is calibrated on: the material, and the size and position of the holes or notches. A person who has it gets a standard made that represents the part and the flaw to be found.
skills.learned: Level III certification in the method; on the job.

skills.name: Tap Testing
skills.what: Finding disbonds and delaminations near the surface of bonded and composite panels by tapping and listening for a dull note. A person who has it taps in a regular grid, marks out the dull area and knows the method's limits.
skills.learned: Composite repair and aircraft maintenance courses; on the job.

skills.name: Bond Testing
skills.what: Finding where adhesive has let go between skin and core or between layers, using low-frequency instruments. A person who has it sets up on a standard with built-in disbonds and maps the unbonded area.
skills.learned: Employer training and certification on bond testers; often added to ultrasonic certification.
tools: Bond testers using pitch-catch, resonance and mechanical impedance

skills.name: Delamination Sizing
skills.what: Mapping and measuring damage found in a laminate, in area and in depth; impact damage is usually wider inside than the dent shows. A person who has it scans beyond the visible mark, finds the edges by signal drop and reports size and ply depth for the repair decision.
skills.learned: Learned with ultrasonic inspection of composites.

skills.name: Laser Shearography
skills.what: Finding disbonds and delaminations by imaging how a surface deforms under a small load from vacuum, heat or vibration. A person who has it applies the load, reads the fringe patterns and marks out defects.
skills.learned: System makers' courses and employer certification.

skills.name: Test Fixture Setup
skills.what: Setting up the fixture that holds and connects a unit under test: mounting it, connecting instruments and cables, loading the right program and running the self-check. A person who has it gets repeatable contact and knows a fixture fault from a product fault.
skills.learned: On the job in a test area; electronics technology programs.

skills.name: Functional Testing
skills.what: Running a product through its functional test: applying power and inputs, checking outputs against limits and recording the result. A person who has it follows the procedure exactly and describes a failure well enough to be diagnosed.
skills.learned: On the job in a test area; electronics technology programs.

skills.name: In-Circuit Test Development
skills.what: Building the test that probes a loaded board net by net for shorts, opens and wrong or missing parts. A person who has it specifies the fixture from the board data, writes and debugs the program and tunes out false failures.
skills.learned: On the job as a test engineer; tester makers' courses.

skills.name: Boundary Scan Testing
skills.what: Testing the connections between chips on a board through the chips' own built-in test cells (IEEE 1149.1). A person who has it builds the scan chain from the design data, generates the tests and reads a failure down to the pin.
skills.learned: On the job as a test engineer or technician; tool makers' courses.

skills.name: Hi-Pot Testing
skills.what: Proving insulation by applying a high voltage between conductors and ground and measuring leakage. A person who has it sets voltage, ramp, dwell and trip limit from the specification and runs the test inside a guarded fixture.
skills.learned: On the job in electrical and electronics test, after electrical safety training.

skills.name: Continuity and Wiring Verification
skills.what: Checking that every wire in a harness or installation goes where the drawing says, with no opens, shorts or crossed pins. A person who has it uses a meter or an automatic tester and finds the fault when one shows.
skills.learned: Electronics and aviation maintenance programs; on the job.

skills.name: Burn-In Testing
skills.what: Running new devices or systems under heat and electrical load for a set time so weak units fail before shipping. A person who has it loads the boards or racks, monitors the run and logs each failure.
skills.learned: On the job in semiconductor and electronics test.

skills.name: Reliability Stress Testing
skills.what: Stressing a product with temperature, vibration, humidity and voltage beyond normal use to find how and when it fails. A person who has it sets up the chamber and monitoring, steps the stress and records each failure for analysis.
skills.learned: On the job in a reliability lab; ASQ's Certified Reliability Engineer covers the theory.

skills.name: Accelerated Life Testing
skills.what: Estimating a product's life in use from tests run at raised stress. A person who has it picks the stress and its model, runs enough samples to failure and fits the life distribution.
skills.learned: Engineering study; ASQ's Certified Reliability Engineer.

skills.name: Vibration and Shock Testing
skills.what: Shaking a product to a specified sine, random or shock profile. A person who has it fixtures the unit, places control and response accelerometers and runs the profile without over-testing.
skills.learned: On the job in an environmental test lab; shaker makers' courses.

skills.name: Thermal Vacuum Testing
skills.what: Cycling a spacecraft or unit between hot and cold in a vacuum chamber to prove it works in space conditions. A person who has it instruments the unit, pumps the chamber down, runs the profile and watches temperatures and pressure.
skills.learned: On the job in a space test lab.

skills.name: EMC Testing
skills.what: Measuring the electromagnetic noise a product emits and its immunity to outside interference. A person who has it sets up the unit and antennas in a chamber, runs emissions and immunity scans to the standard and finds the source of a failure.
skills.learned: Electrical engineering study; on the job in a test lab.

skills.name: Spectrum Analyzer Measurement
skills.what: Measuring a radio signal's power across frequency. A person who has it sets span, resolution bandwidth and reference level and reads power, harmonics and spurious signals.
skills.learned: Electronics technology and engineering programs; on the job in radio-frequency test.

skills.name: Vector Network Analyzer Measurement
skills.what: Measuring how a cable, antenna, filter or amplifier reflects and passes signals across frequency. A person who has it calibrates at the test ports and reads return loss, insertion loss and phase.
skills.learned: Electronics technology and engineering programs; on the job in radio-frequency test.

skills.name: Test Automation Programming
skills.what: Writing the program that runs a test and gathers its data. A person who has it controls instruments, sequences the steps, checks limits, logs results and builds an operator screen.
skills.learned: Engineering and electronics programs; test software makers' courses and developer certifications.
tools: Graphical and text test programming environments

skills.name: Power Electronics Functional Test
skills.what: Testing inverters, converters and chargers under power: isolation, control signals, switching, efficiency and behavior under load. A person who has it connects the unit safely, runs the sequence and reads a failure back to a board or module.
skills.learned: On the job in power electronics test, after high-voltage safety qualification.

skills.name: Dynamometer Testing
skills.what: Running a motor, drive unit or engine against a controlled load to measure torque, speed, power and efficiency. A person who has it mounts and aligns the unit, runs the test points and watches temperatures and vibration.
skills.learned: On the job in a test lab.

skills.name: Vehicle Roll and Brake Test
skills.what: Driving a finished vehicle on rollers at the end of the line to check acceleration, braking, transmission and stability systems. A person who has it follows the test sequence and reads the pass and fail results.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Squeak and Rattle Testing
skills.what: Finding unwanted noises in a vehicle by shaking it or driving it over a rough track, then curing them. A person who has it locates the source by ear and with listening tools.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly and quality.

skills.name: Water Leak Testing
skills.what: Soaking a finished vehicle in a spray booth and checking the cabin and luggage space for water. A person who has it knows the usual leak paths, finds the entry point and sends it for sealing.
skills.learned: On the job in vehicle final assembly.

skills.name: Headlamp Aiming
skills.what: Setting a vehicle's headlamp beams to the correct height and direction on an aiming machine. A person who has it positions the aimer, reads the pattern and adjusts each lamp.
skills.learned: On the job at the end of a vehicle assembly line.

skills.name: ADAS Calibration
skills.what: Calibrating a vehicle's driver-assistance cameras and radars to its direction of travel after assembly. A person who has it sets up the targets, runs the routine through the diagnostic tool and confirms each sensor has learned.
skills.learned: On the job at the end of a vehicle assembly line; automotive programs.

skills.name: Hot Fire Testing
skills.what: Firing a rocket engine or stage on a test stand. A person who has it prepares the stand, follows the countdown procedure step by step, watches the limits that abort a test and makes the stand safe afterwards.
skills.learned: On the job at a rocket test site.

skills.name: Engine Acceptance Testing
skills.what: Running a newly built engine through the test that proves it meets specification before delivery. A person who has it sets up the test, runs the profile and reviews thrust or power, pressures, temperatures and vibration against limits.
skills.learned: On the job in an engine test cell.

skills.name: Propellant Loading
skills.what: Loading propellants and high-pressure gases into a vehicle or test stand. A person who has it follows the loading procedure, controls flow and pressure and wears the protection the propellant requires.
skills.learned: On the job at a launch or test site, with hazardous operations training.

skills.name: Cryogenic Propellant Handling
skills.what: Working with liquid oxygen, liquid methane and other cryogenic fluids. A person who has it chills lines down before flow, keeps oxygen systems free of oil and grease and protects against cold burns and trapped liquid.
skills.learned: On the job at a propulsion test or launch site, with cryogenic and oxygen safety training.

skills.name: Test Telemetry Review
skills.what: Watching the live data from a test or flight and reviewing it afterwards. A person who has it knows the normal range of each channel, spots a trend before it reaches a limit and pulls the data for analysis.
skills.learned: On the job in test operations.

skills.name: Pitot-Static System Testing
skills.what: Leak-checking an aircraft's pitot and static lines and verifying altimeter and airspeed readings with a test set. A person who has it connects the adapters, applies pressure slowly and records the results. FAA rules require the altimeter system check every 24 months for instrument flight.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant or avionics training; on the job at a repair station.

skills.name: ARINC 429 Data Bus Testing
skills.what: Checking the data bus that links civil aircraft avionics. A person who has it reads and sends labels with a bus analyzer and finds a unit or wire that is not talking.
skills.learned: Avionics programs and on the job.

skills.name: MIL-STD-1553 Data Bus Testing
skills.what: Checking the data bus used in military aircraft and spacecraft. A person who has it monitors traffic between the bus controller and remote terminals, checks waveform and termination and finds the faulty stub or unit.
skills.learned: Military avionics training and on the job.

skills.name: Radar System Testing
skills.what: Testing a radar's transmitter, receiver and antenna against specification. A person who has it measures power, sensitivity and pattern with test equipment and aligns the system.
skills.learned: Military electronics training or an electronics technology degree; on the job at a defense plant.

skills.name: Firmware Loading
skills.what: Programming a board or unit with its released firmware and configuration at a test station. A person who has it connects the programmer, picks the released version for the part number, confirms the load verified and records version and serial number.
skills.learned: On the job at a test or assembly station.

skills.name: Test Procedure Writing
skills.what: Writing the procedure a test is run to: setup, steps, limits, hold points and what to record. A person who has it turns a requirement into steps a technician can follow without asking, with pass and fail stated for every one, and has it reviewed and released.
skills.learned: On the job as a senior test technician or test engineer.

skills.name: Data Acquisition Setup
skills.what: Instrumenting a test: mounting and wiring thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, accelerometers and load cells, and setting up the system that records them. A person who has it sets ranges, sample rates and filters, checks every channel end to end before the test and knows a bad channel from a real reading.
skills.learned: Electronics and engineering technology programs; on the job as a test technician.
tools: Thermocouples, pressure transducers and strain gauges

skills.name: Hardware-in-the-Loop Testing
skills.what: Testing a controller by connecting it to a real-time simulation of the machine it will run, so faults and edge cases can be tried without the hardware. A person who has it builds the test bench, maps signals between controller and model, automates the test cases and traces a failure to controller, model or wiring.
skills.learned: Engineering degree and on the job as a test engineer; simulator makers' courses.
tools: Signal conditioning and fault insertion units

skills.name: 3D CAD Modeling
skills.what: Modeling parts and assemblies in a parametric 3D CAD system and making drawings from them. A person who has it builds models that update cleanly when a dimension changes, works in solids and surfaces to the company's modeling standards and produces drawings a shop can work from.
skills.learned: Community-college drafting and engineering programs; the CAD makers certify users.

skills.name: 2D CAD Drafting
skills.what: Two-dimensional drafting in CAD: layers, blocks, dimension styles and plotted sheets. A person who has it produces accurate layouts, schematics and detail drawings to a drafting standard.
skills.learned: Community-college drafting programs; the CAD makers certify users.

skills.name: Engineering Drawing Creation
skills.what: Making a drawing that fully defines a part: views, sections, dimensions, tolerances, notes and title block, to a drafting standard such as ASME Y14.5. A person who has it leaves nothing for the shop to guess.
skills.learned: Drafting and engineering programs. The American Design Drafting Association certifies drafters.

skills.name: CAD Assembly Modeling
skills.what: Putting part models together into an assembly with mates or constraints. A person who has it structures subassemblies, checks interference and motion and produces the bill of material.
skills.learned: Drafting and engineering programs.

skills.name: PDM and PLM Use
skills.what: Working with design data under control: checking files out and in, revising, routing changes for approval and finding the released revision. A person who has it never builds from an unreleased drawing.
skills.learned: On the job; software makers' courses.
tools: Product data and lifecycle management systems

skills.name: Design for Manufacturability
skills.what: Shaping a design so it can be made and assembled reliably at reasonable cost: fewer parts, sensible tolerances, features a process can actually produce. A person who has it reviews a design with the people who will make it and changes it early.
skills.learned: Engineering study; on the job between design and manufacturing.

skills.name: Finite Element Analysis
skills.what: Predicting stress, deflection, vibration and heat flow in a part with a computer model. A person who has it builds the mesh, applies loads and constraints that match reality and checks the answer against a hand calculation or test.
skills.learned: Engineering degree; software makers' courses.

skills.name: CNC Program Verification
skills.what: Checking a CNC program in a virtual copy of the machine before it runs. A person who has it builds the machine, fixture and stock setup, runs the posted code and clears collisions, gouges and excess material.
skills.learned: On the job as a CNC programmer; the simulation software makers run courses.

skills.name: Circuit Design and Schematic Capture
skills.what: Designing an electronic circuit and drawing it as a schematic: choosing parts, working out values and margins, simulating where it matters and producing a clean netlist and bill of material. A person who has it reads datasheets closely and draws a schematic another engineer can review.
skills.learned: Electrical engineering degree or electronics technology program; on the job.

skills.name: PCB Layout
skills.what: Turning a schematic into a board that can be built: stack-up, placement, routing, power and ground, controlled impedance and clearances, then the fabrication and assembly files. A person who has it lays out for signal integrity and for the factory at once and clears the design rule check honestly.
skills.learned: On the job as a designer or engineer; IPC's Certified Interconnect Designer (CID) course.

skills.name: Electrical Controls Design
skills.what: Designing a machine's electrical system and drawing it: power distribution, motor circuits, controller I/O, safety circuits, panel layout and the bill of material. A person who has it sizes wire, breakers and enclosures to code and produces a drawing set a panel shop can build from without calling.
skills.learned: Electrical engineering or technology study; on the job in a controls group. UL 508A and NFPA 79 set the rules.
tools: Schematics, panel layouts and wire lists

skills.name: Fixture and Tooling Design
skills.what: Designing the fixtures, jigs, gauges and assembly tools that hold and locate a part while it is made or checked. A person who has it locates on the part's datums, clamps without distorting it, leaves room for the cutter or the hand and designs the tool to be built and maintained by the shop it is for.
skills.learned: Engineering degree or a toolmaker's apprenticeship followed by design work; on the job.

skills.name: Data Analysis and Scripting
skills.what: Pulling production, test or equipment data and answering a question with it: querying a database, cleaning the data, plotting it and automating the report. A person who has it writes a short script instead of repeating a spreadsheet by hand and checks the answer against what the floor knows.
skills.learned: Engineering study and on the job; online courses in Python and SQL.

skills.name: Requirements Management
skills.what: Writing down what a system must do and keeping each requirement tied to where it came from and how it will be proven. A person who has it writes requirements that can be tested, flows them down to subsystems and keeps the trace intact as the design changes.
skills.learned: Engineering degree and on the job; INCOSE's systems engineering certifications.

skills.name: Verification Planning
skills.what: Deciding how each requirement will be proven, by test, analysis, inspection or demonstration, and planning the campaign that does it. A person who has it builds the verification matrix, sets what counts as passing before the test is run and closes each requirement with evidence.
skills.learned: On the job as a systems or test engineer; INCOSE's systems engineering certifications.

skills.name: Bulk Chemical Transfer
skills.what: Moving liquids and gases between trucks, railcars, tanks and process: lining up valves, connecting and grounding hoses, starting pumps and watching levels. A person who has it walks the line before starting, never leaves a transfer unattended and knows what to do when a hose or a level alarm fails.
skills.learned: On the job as an outside operator; process technology programs at community colleges. Loading and unloading hazardous materials needs training under 49 CFR 172.

skills.name: Batch Reactor Operation
skills.what: Running a batch through a reactor: charging raw materials in order, heating or cooling to the recipe, holding, sampling and discharging. A person who has it controls an exotherm by feed rate and cooling, keeps the batch record as each step is done and knows the safe state to go to when something is wrong.
skills.learned: On the job at a chemical plant; process technology (PTEC) associate degree programs.
tools: Charging pumps, scales and flow meters

skills.name: Distillation Column Operation
skills.what: Running a distillation column to separate a mixture: starting it up, setting reflux, reboil and pressure and holding product purity as feed changes. A person who has it reads the temperature profile, sees flooding or weeping coming and brings the column back without going off specification.
skills.learned: On the job at a chemical plant or refinery; process technology (PTEC) associate degree programs.

skills.name: Distributed Control System Operation
skills.what: Running a continuous or batch plant from the control room: watching the unit through its control system, moving setpoints, answering alarms and directing the operators outside. A person who has it keeps the unit steady through an upset, knows which alarm matters first and takes the plant to a safe state when it must.
skills.learned: Years as an outside operator on the same unit, then board training on a simulator and beside a qualified board operator.

Installing or building one named product or system: a weapon, sensor, avionics unit, airframe section or motor variant. Too narrow to be a skill of its own; the fastening, wiring, sealing and rigging skills cover the work, and no career used these.
Knowledge of, or work on, one company's named product. Each was on one or two career paths; those paths keep the transferable skills beside it.
Launch, flight and mission operations: not manufacturing work.
Theory, background knowledge or a topic too vague to be shown or assessed.
Supervision, planning, clerical and warehouse work, and general awareness topics. The catalogue is for technical skills of the plant floor and its engineering office.
Design, analysis and reference software, and CAD techniques, that no career used. The CAD and CAM packages careers do use are kept.
A real method or process, but on no career, and no career in the catalogue plainly needs it.
